steps: In a large pot, bring 6 cups of water to a boil. Add Brussels sprouts and blanch in the boiling water for 1 minute. Remove from boiling water and run under cold water to stop the cooking. Dry the sprouts with a clean towel.

Trim the stem on the Brussels sprouts and slice in half lengthwise. Using the slicing blade on a food processor, process the Brussels sprouts to shred them. You can also do this with the slicing side of a box grater or with a very sharp knife.
In a medium bowl, whisk together scallions, vinegar, mustard, soy sauce, low- or no-calorie sweetener, mayonnaise and black pepper.
Add the shredded Brussels sprouts and toasted almonds to the dressing and mix well.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Asian Turkey Burgers
description: Looking for a way to spice up your burgers? Then this recipe is just for you! Sauces used in this recipe like oyster sauce, Thai chili garlic and Sriracha can be found in the ethnic food aisle at most grocery stores.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 70mg 23%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 310mg 7%
ingredients: 1 tbsp oyster sauce (if you cannot find oyster sauce, sub 1 Tbsp. reduced sodium soy sauce)
2 stalks green onion (scallion) (minced, white and green part)
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.

In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, scallions, garlic, oyster sauce, chili garlic paste, sesame oil, grated ginger, lime juice, salt (optional), and pepper. Form into 6 patties and refrigerate until ready to grill, at least 15 minutes.
Grill burgers for 5-7 minutes on each side or until the internal temperature of the burger is 165 degrees F.
To assemble the burgers, combine the yogurt and Siracha in a small bowl. Layer each burger between two leaves of lettuce with a scant 1 Tbsp. yogurt mixture and 3 cucumber slices.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Budget-Friendly Braised Chicken Thighs with Mushrooms
description: Healthy eating can be done on a budget and this dinner proves it! Chicken thighs are less expensive than chicken breast and can be a nice change. This makes a tasty, low-carb, budget-friendly meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 25g; Potassium 290mg 6%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs (boneless, skinless)
steps: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs and sauté for 3 minutes per side. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add margarine to pan and melt. Add onion and sauté for 2 minutes. Add mushrooms and sauté for 3-5 minutes until liquid is released; stirring frequently.
Add balsamic vinegar to pan and cook with mushrooms for 1 minute. Add chicken thighs back to pan and place mushrooms on top of chicken. Pour chicken broth into pan.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the pan with a heavy, tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 25 minutes.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Chicken Chili
description: This chili is perfect for a fall dinner and it’s full of vitamin C, protein and fiber. Feel free to experiment with different beans such as black or Great Northern beans here.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 40mg 13%; Sodium 630mg 27%; Total Carbohydrate 31g 11%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 23g; Potassium 904mg 19%
ingredients: 1 (15 ounce) can navy or great northern beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: Spray a large soup pot with cooking spray. Add chicken and sauté over medium heat for 7 minutes or until done. Remove from pan.
Add onions and green peppers and sauté over medium-high heat for 3 minutes or onions until clear. Add garlic and sauté 30 more seconds.
Add remaining ingredients along with cooked chicken and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Chicken Piccata
description: Chicken piccata is a classic Italian dish featuring briny capers and fresh lemon. The chicken is pounded thin and lightly breaded with breadcrumbs making it tender and crispy. This budget-friendly recipe is quick and easy to make. Serve over a bed of spinach and with a side of whole-wheat pasta for a light Italian dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 150mg 50%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 35g; Potassium 560mg 12%
steps: Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F. Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray and set aside.
Slice the chicken breast in half lengthwise and then pound to 1/4-inch thickness. Season each chicken breast with salt and ground black pepper.

Set up three wide bowls or flat-bottom containers. Fill the first bowl with the whole wheat flour, the second bowl with the egg and 1 tsp lemon juice, and the third bowl with the breadcrumbs and Italian seasoning. Whisk the egg and lemon juice together. Combine the breadcrumbs and Italian seasoning and mix well.

Dredge one chicken breast in the flour and shake off the excess. Then dip the chicken breast in the egg, and then coat in the breadcrumb mixture. Place on the baking sheet. Repeat this process for the remaining three chicken breasts.

Spray the top of each chicken breast with cooking spray and bake for 8 minutes. Turn the chicken breasts over and bake for 5 more minutes. Ensure that the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
While the chicken is baking, heat the oil and a generous amount of cooking spray over medium heat in a small nonstick skillet. Add the capers and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add about 1 tbsp lemon juice and cook until the lemon juice is completely reduced. Add the chicken broth and simmer until reduced by half. Stir in the parsley.
Remove the chicken from the oven and serve with 1 Tbsp. of sauce drizzled over the chicken.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Chicken Sausage and Cabbage Skillet
description: This budget-friendly recipe comes together quickly for a week night dinner, with the flavors of fall coming from the apples, onions and shredded cabbage!
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 18g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 14g; Potassium 340mg 7%
ingredients: 3 links fully cooked roasted garlic chicken sausage (sliced)
2 small Granny Smith or other tart apple (peeled and grated (use large hole on grater))
steps: Add oil and a generous amount of cooking spray to a large sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Sauté sausage until beginning to brown. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add apples, onion and cabbage to the pan and sauté for 8-10 minutes or until cabbage is soft and beginning to lightly brown.
Add sausage back to the pan and remaining ingredients. Sauté until liquid reduced.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Cilantro Lime Roasted Chicken
description: Cilantro and lime make a fresh and zesty flavor combination in this chicken dish. We start with a whole chicken and break it down into 2 breasts, 2 thighs, two drumsticks, and 2 wings. Butchers at grocery stores will usually break down a whole chicken for you, or you can purchase 2-3 of chicken pieces.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 18g; Potassium 170mg 4%
steps: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a baking dish with cooking spray.
Remove the skin from the chicken and arrange in a single layer in the baking pan.

In a small bowl, whisk together the cilantro, lime zest, lime juice, honey, garlic, ground black pepper and salt. Pour the mixture evenly over the chicken and bake for 45-50 minutes or until the internal temperature of the largest piece of chicken is 165 degrees.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Deluxe Chicken Nachos
description: You can make these nachos as spicy as you want by purchasing the salsa at the heat level you prefer. If you like it even hotter, top the yogurt with a couple dashes of hot sauce.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 530mg 23%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 21g; Potassium 720mg 15%
ingredients: 8 small corn tortillas (cut into 6 pieces each)
1 lbs chicken breasts (boneless, skinless, cooked and shredded)
1/2 cup Mexican style cheese (reduced fat, shredded)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Coat one large or two small baking sheet(s) with cooking spray.
Lay cut corn tortillas in one layer on the baking sheet(s). Spray the top with cooking spray. Lightly sprinkle with salt (optional).
Bake for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or until the chips are slightly golden brown and crispy. Remove from oven and pour into a baking dish coated with cooking spray. Set aside.
Mix fat-free refried beans with chicken broth and pour over the baked tortilla chips.
Top the beans with the shredded chicken and then with the reduced fat cheese.
Place on the top rack of the oven and bake for 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted and starting to turn golden brown.
Remove from the oven and divide the nachos among eight plates. Top each plate with diced tomatoes, salsa, 1/4 avocado, lettuce and yogurt.

title: Budget-Friendly Egg, Ham and Spinach Sandwich
description: Need a quick, delicious and inexpensive meal for breakfast or dinner? Here is your answer. Eggs are a cheap, high-quality protein source and are fine to eat in moderation.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 190mg 63%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 14g; Potassium 320mg 7%
ingredients: 2 oz lower sodium deli-style ham (4 thin slices)
4 whole wheat sandwich thins (1-1/2 oz each, toasted)
steps: Spray a nonstick oven-proof skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Add ham slices and cook for 1 minute per side. Remove from pan and set aside.
Spray the pan with cooking spray and add the olive oil. Add the spinach to the pan and sauté until wilted. Sprinkle with garlic powder and pepper and combine well. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Crack the eggs into the pan; break the yolk with a spatula to make it run. Cook until the egg starts to firm, about 30 – 60 seconds. Flip the egg and continue cooking until done.
Place an egg on one half of each sandwich thin, top with a slice of ham and ¼ of the spinach. Top with the other half of the sandwich thin.

title: Budget-Friendly Greek Salad and Grilled Shrimp Pitas
description: Serve this dish with a cup of cold gazpacho soup or with sautéed zucchini seasoned with lemon juice and oregano.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 230mg 5%
ingredients: 1/2 large, or 1 small cucumber(s) (peeled and sliced)
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.
In a large bowl, toss together lettuce, onion, cucumber, feta cheese, olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano.
Fill each pita pocket half with 1/4 of lettuce mixture. Set aside.
Season shrimp with salt (optional), ground black pepper and cayenne pepper. Spray shrimp with cooking spray.
Grill shrimp for 3-4 minutes on each side. Remove from grill and add 3 shrimp to each pita.

title: Budget-Friendly Hearty Cabbage Soup
description: This veggie-loaded, high-fiber soup is more satisfying than traditional cabbage soup because of the addition of beans and turkey sausage. It also freezes well, so freeze half and use it during a busy week when you don’t have much time to cook.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 25mg 8%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 8g; Potassium 420mg 9%
ingredients: 40 oz low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, low-sodium)
1 (15.5-ounce) can canned navy or great northern beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: Spray a large soup pot with cooking spray. Add celery, onion and carrots and sauté over medium-high heat for 3 minutes or onions until clear. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add turkey sausage and cook until brown, about 6-7 minutes. Add celery, onions and carrots back to pan and mix.
Add remaining ingredients and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.

title: Budget-Friendly Herb Garlic Meatloaf
description:
This savory budget-friendly meat loaf is just as good as classic meatloaf. Our diabetes-friendly version is made with lean ground turkey and is seasoned with fresh herbs and garlic. For a complete meal, serve with over roasted sweet potatoes (they can roast alongside the meatloaf in the oven) and a nonstarchy vegetable side or simple green salad.

Powered by Homemade
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 70mg 23%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 20g; Potassium 320mg 7%
steps: Pre heat oven to 375 degrees F. Coat a loaf pan with cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, break up the piece of whole wheat bread into pea-sized pieces. Add egg and mix well.
Add turkey, garlic, oregano, basil, 1/4 cup ketchup, salt (optional) and ground black pepper. Mix well.
Press the turkey mixture into the loaf pan tightly. Put in oven to bake for 20 minutes.
While meatloaf is baking, whisk together remaining 1/4 cup of ketchup, balsamic vinegar and hot sauce (optional).

After the meatloaf has baked for 20 minutes, pour the ketchup and balsamic glaze over the meatloaf. Return to the oven to bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the internal temperature of the meatloaf is 165 degrees F.
Let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes, then slice into 6 equal portions.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Kale and Sausage Sauté
description: This simple, low carb entree is packed with protein, fiber, and vegetables. Best of all, it can be ready in under 30 minutes!
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 35mg 12%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 310mg 7%
ingredients: 3 links (about 3 oz each) Italian style chicken sausage (diced)
steps: Add olive oil to a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Add diced sausage and onion and sauté until onions begin to turn golden brown.
Add the kale and chicken broth and sauté until kale softens.
Add remaining ingredients and sauté 3-4 more minutes to heat the beans through.
Serving Suggestion: Serve with a side of brown rice to round out the meal.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Mediterranean Fish Stew
description: This Mediterranean fish stew costs a little more than $10 for 4 servings, but it can be a real treat and is great for the chilly winter weather!
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats -0.02g; Cholesterol 105mg 35%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 0.99g 2%; Protein 20g; Potassium 1030mg 22%
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
1 (28-oz can) canned crushed tomatoes (no salt added)
steps: Add olive oil to a soup pot over medium heat. Add onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, basil and oregano. Sauté until onions begin to turn clear.
Add crushed tomato and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10 minutes or until vegetables are soft.
Gently stir in cod and shrimp and cook for 5 minutes or until seafood is cooked through.

title: Budget-Friendly Pork Chops with Peach Salsa
description:
Take advantage of seasonal produce and pair this mouth-watering salsa sweet-and-savory salsa with pork chops. It would also be great over chicken or fish. For a more intensely flavored salsa, grill the peaches, bell pepper, and onion along side the pork chop before chopping and mixing them together for the salsa.

Powered by Homemade
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 28g; Potassium 640mg 14%
ingredients: 1 lb (4 chops) lean boneless pork chops
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill. Season pork chops with pepper, garlic powder and oregano. Grill pork chops over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side or until done.
In a small bowl, mix together the peaches, bell pepper, red onion, vinegar, oil, and cilantro.
Top each cooked pork chop with about 1/4 cup salsa mixture and serve.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Roasted Veggie Tacos
description: Trying to eat a meatless, veggie-packed meal once a week? This recipe gives you all the flavor of tacos, but with so much more fiber and vegetables. Top them with avocado slices for extra flavor if you’d like.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 180mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 506mg 11%
ingredients: 1 cup black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)
1/2 cup queso fresco ((or reduced-fat shredded cheddar))
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place zucchini, carrots, onions, and red pepper on baking sheet. Add olive oil and garlic; toss to coat. Bake for 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.

While vegetables are baking, heat a medium sauté pan over medium heat. Spray with cooking spray. Add tomato and sauté for 1 minute. Add beans, chili powder, cumin and pepper and sauté for 2 minutes. Add cooked vegetables to pan and mix well.
Serve 1/2 cup veggie mixture in each taco and top with lettuce and cheese.

title: Budget-Friendly Salmon Burgers
description: These burgers are a good way to spice up your menu! They are packed with heart-healthy salmon, plus some veggies. To keep the carbohydrate count low, these are served over bibb lettuce instead of on a bun. Serve these burgers with a green salad drizzled with a sesame ginger vinaigrette for a light, refreshing meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 70mg 23%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 280mg 6%
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and chopped)
steps: Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F. Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray and set aside.
Place the onion, garlic, bell pepper, and Thai curry paste in a large food processor and blend until smooth.
Add the salmon and puree until smooth. Add the egg and cilantro and puree until incorporated.
Scoop the mixture in 1/2 cup portions onto the baking sheet and press lightly to form a patty. Repeat to make 6 patties.
Spray the top of each patty with cooking spray and bake for 15 minutes.
Serve each salmon burger in a lettuce leaf and top each with 1 Tbsp. sliced scallions.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Slow-Cooker Chicken & Sweet Potatoes
description: No time to cook? Try this slow-cooker chicken for dinner. The sweet potatoes, Dijon mustard and brown sugar make for a unique and tasty flavor. Adding a side of simple steamed broccoli and cauliflower makes this a complete meal that requires less than 15 minutes of active prep time.
serving_size: 1 chicken thigh with 2-3 sweet potato rounds and 1 cup broccoli and cauliflower mix
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 39g 14%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 28g; Potassium 700mg 15%
ingredients: 1 lbs sweet potatoes (peeled and sliced into large rounds)
4 cup fresh or frozen broccoli and cauliflower florets (steamed)
steps: Place chicken in a slow cooker. Top chicken with onions and sweet potatoes.
Add the chicken broth, brown sugar blend, thyme, mustard, and bay leaf. Cook on low for 5-6 hours or until chicken is done.
Remove bay leaf and serve with broccoli and cauliflower.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Stuffed Peppers
description: Make this whole dish the night before and hold in the refrigerator until you are ready to serve. Just heat them up in the oven or in the microwave and you’ll have dinner for the whole family in no time. They’re also delicious when eaten cold!
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 1.5g 2%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 260mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 26g; Potassium 390mg 8%
ingredients: 6 small bell peppers ((any color or assorted colors))
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Add lentils, water, ginger, garlic and turmeric to a medium sauce pan. Bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer, partially covered for 20 minutes. Set aside to cool.
While lentils are cooking, mix ground chicken, cilantro, salt, ground black pepper and cayenne pepper in a medium bowl and set aside.

Cut the tops off of the peppers and cut out seed pod (save the tops). Clean out the ribs and any seeds from the inside of the peppers and line the peppers cut side up in a baking dish. Set the tops off to the side. (Note: If the peppers won’t sit upright, trim just a little bit off the bottom of the peppers to even it out so it will sit up straight. Try not to cut a hole in the bottom so the mixture inside does not fall out).
Once the lentils have cooled, stir them in to the chicken mixture and mix well to incorporate.
Fill each pepper with the chicken and lentil mixture but do not pack the mixture in tightly. Just gently fill to the top.
Place each pepper top back on to the peppers filled with the chicken and lentil mixture, then pour the chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
Bake for 1 hour or until the internal temperature of the chicken mixture is 165 degrees.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Summer Vegetable Frittata
description: This frittata is a great way to get more veggies into your day and can be enjoyed for brunch or dinner. By using a combination of egg whites and whole eggs, you cut back on some of the saturated fat and cholesterol.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 530mg 11%
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Add olive oil to an oven safe, non-stick, sauté pan over medium high heat.
Add mushrooms and sauté until all of the liquid from the mushrooms is evaporated.
Add bell pepper, onion and spinach and sauté until vegetables are softened and liquid is evaporated.
Whisk eggs, egg whites, milk, salt (optional), pepper, cayenne pepper and basil in a medium bowl. Pour over vegetables and stir until eggs start to set.
Smooth the top of the frittata with a spatula, and put in oven to bake for 20 minutes or until eggs are set.
Slide the frittata out of the pan onto a plate and slice into 8 pie slices.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Tuna Pasta Salad
description: You could try this tuna salad without the pasta and serve it on a bed of lettuce or on top of a hearty salad. This quick and budget-friendly meal makes a healthy lunch or dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 16g; Potassium 260mg 6%
ingredients: 11 oz flavor fresh tuna (pouch in water)
steps: Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt. Drain pasta and rinse under cold water.
In a medium bowl combine remaining ingredients. Add pasta and toss to coat. Serve.

title: Budget-Friendly Vegetable Stew with Whole Wheat Dumplings
description: What’s better during the fall than a warm, tasty soup? This budget-friendly recipe is fairly easy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 25mg 8%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 30g 11%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 520mg 11%
ingredients: 4 cup kale (chopped, 1 bunch stemmed and chopped)
steps: Add oil to a large soup pot over medium-high heat.

Add fennel, onion and celery to oil and sauté until onions turn clear (around 4-5 minutes). Add butternut squash, sage, chicken broth, water, 1 tsp salt (optional), 1/2 tsp black pepper and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer.
Simmer stew for 20 minutes, then add kale and simmer 10 more minutes.
While stew is simmering, whisk together all dumpling ingredients to form a stiff batter. Set aside.
After kale simmers for 10 minutes remove bay leaf.

Use a 1/4 cup measure to scoop dumplings on top of stew to make 8 dumplings. Do not stir once dumplings have been added to the top of the stew. Cover and reduce to a low simmer for 10 minutes until dumplings are cooked through and puffed.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Budget-Friendly Veggie Burgers with Mango Slaw
description: Serve this vegetarian dish with sliced tomato and fresh mozzarella salad.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 35g 13%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 11g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 422mg 9%
ingredients: 1 med unripe mango (peeled, seeded and shredded)
steps: Coat a large non-stick sauté pan with cooking spray. Set aside.

Combine cannellini beans, onion, garlic, mushrooms, carrots, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, oatmeal, Montreal steak seasoning and salt (optional) in a food processor. Pulse several times until mixture is combined but not a paste.
Divide burger mixture into 6 equal portions, form into patties.
Heat prepared sauté pan over medium high heat. Sauté burgers on each side 6-8 minutes. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine shredded mango, coleslaw mix, rice wine vinegar and olive oil. Toss to coat.
Add a burger to a lettuce leaf, top with 3/4 cup coleslaw mixture.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Bulgogi (Grilled Korean Beef)
description: The marinade for this grilled beef is super easy to throw together. This recipe calls for beef tenderloin, which is a lean cut.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 310mg 7%
ingredients: 3 stalks green onion (scallion) ((white and green parts), chopped)
1 tbsp honey or 2 packets sugar substitute
steps: Wrap the beef in plastic wrap and freeze until firm (but not rock hard). Once firm, slice the beef thinly into long strips. Place in a baking dish.

In a small bowl, whisk together the scallions, garlic, rice wine vinegar, water, soy sauce, sweetener (honey or sugar substitute), and pepper. Pour the mixture over the beef and let it marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, up to 2 hours. While the beef is marinating, preheat an indoor or outdoor grill.
Remove the beef from the marinade and shake off any excess marinade. Grill beef for 2-3 minutes on each side or until it is cooked to a medium-well doneness.
Steam the vegetables and serve the beef over the steamed vegetables.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Butternut Squash Gratin
description: This rich side dish is oh-so-creamy and satisfyingly cheesy but 1 serving is still less than 100 calories.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 5g; Potassium 423mg 9%
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Cut the squash in half lengthwise and place it face down in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Pour the water over the squash and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove the squash from the pan and drain the water. Coat the baking dish with cooking spray.
Remove the seeds and scoop the flesh of the squash out of the skin. Add the squash flesh back to the prepared baking dish, breaking it up into even sized pieces.

Add oil to a sauté pan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir to combine. Cook the oil and flour mixture for two minutes then whisk in the fat-free half and half. Bring to a boil, whisking frequently.
Stir in 1/4 cup of the parmesan cheese, the ground black pepper and the thyme. Stir until cheese is melted.
Pour the sauce over the butternut squash and sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup of cheese over the top. Bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown and bubbling.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Butternut Squash Stew with Chickpeas
description: This hearty stew features butternut squash, a type of winter squash that comes into season during the cooler months of the year. Make this on the weekend and pack the leftovers for lunch during the week.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 700mg 15%
ingredients: 1/2 lbs red potatoes (unpeeled and cut into quarters)
1 cup low sodium chicken broth (low-fat, reduced-sodium)
1 (14 ounce) can canned diced tomatoes (undrained, try fire roasted for more flavor)
1/8 tsp Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 (15 ounce) can chickpeas (garbanzo beans) (drained and rinsed)
2 tbsp natural creamy peanut butter (stirred well until smooth)
steps: Prepare the butternut squash. Place the whole squash on the floor or rack of a microwave oven. Microwave the squash for 5 minutes. Carefully remove and let cool until it’s cool enough to handle. With a sharp knife, cut the squash in half crosswise. Peel the skin off each half with the knife, cutting close to remove the skin only. Cut each half lengthwise. Remove the squash seeds from the bottom half of the squash and discard. Cut all the squash into 1-inch chunks. Set aside. This process makes cutting tough butternut squash easier as it helps loosen the skin.

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and sauté for 5-6 minutes. Add the butternut squash and potatoes and stir to coat with the onions and garlic. Add the broth, tomatoes with juice, oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to boil. Lower the heat to a simmer, cover, and cook on medium-low heat for about 20 minutes, until squash and potatoes are tender. Some of the squash may become very soft.
Gently mix the chickpeas and peanut butter and cook for 5 minutes. Garnish with chopped parsley.

title: Cabbage Salad
description: Cabbage is an Irish staple. Serve this salad with Bangers and Mash for a complete Irish treat on St. Patrick’s Day!
nutrients_raw: Calories 45; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 180mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 0g; Protein 1g; Potassium 6mg <1%
ingredients: 1 tsp low- or no-calorie sweetener (or 1/2 tsp)
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the light mayonnaise, rice wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, low- or no-calorie sweetener, and poppy seeds.
Fold the cabbage into the dressing and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving to allow cabbage to marinate. (You can serve it instantly as well but it is better if allowed to marinate)

title: Caesar-Style Salad with Rustic Croutons
description: Who doesn’t love Caesar salad? This salad makes a great nonstarchy vegetable side that you can enjoy with just about any entrée!
serving_size: 1 cup salad + 2 tbsp dressing + 1/2 cup croutons
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 4g; Potassium 190mg 4%
ingredients: 2 slice whole wheat bread or French bread (torn into 1/2-inch pieces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.

In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, mayonnaise, garlic powder, salt (optional) and pepper (optional) to taste. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour in order to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, place the bread pieces on a baking sheet and bake 8 minutes or until slightly firm. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Place mixed greens in a salad bowl, add dressing and cheese, and toss gently, yet thoroughly to coat. Season lightly with salt and pepper, if desired. Add croutons, toss gently and serve immediately.
*Note: Optional salt and pepper is not included in the nutrition information above.

title: Caprese Kabobs
description: This easy appetizer is perfect for summer and uses garden fresh ingredients. These kabobs are packed with flavor and low in carbohydrates. They also look beautiful on a serving platter and are sure to impress guests!
nutrients_raw: Calories 30; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 5mg <1%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 0.99g; Potassium 0mg 0%
ingredients: 18 whole fresh mozzarella balls (1/4 ounce each)
steps: Place 1 grape tomato, 1 basil leaf, and 1 mozzarella ball on each bamboo fork. Repeat this process for 18 kabobs. Place the kabobs on a serving platter.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Right before serving, drizzle the dressing over the kabobs to coat evenly.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Caribbean Bean Dip
description: Make this dip and store it in the fridge so you can snack on it with some fresh veggies throughout the week.
serving_size: 3½ Tbsp dip + 4 celery sticks + 4 carrot sticks
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 1.5g 2%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 90mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 330mg 7%
ingredients: 1 (15.5 ounce) can organic black beans (drained and rinsed)
4 med carrots (cut in half into smaller sticks)
steps: Puree all ingredients except the green onion in a blender until smooth. Top with green onion.
Serve with celery and carrot sticks.

title: Cauliflower "Mac" and Cheese with Lobster
description: This lower-carbohydrate version of luxurious lobster mac and cheese features crisp-topped, cheesy cauliflower florets and tender poached lobster.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 520mg 11%
ingredients: 1 head cauliflower (trimmed into florets (8 cups florets))
2 whole 4-oz frozen lobster tails or 1 cup chopped imitation lobster meat
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Coat a 9x13-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.
Place cauliflower florets in a large microwave-safe dish. Pour 1 cup of water over the cauliflower and cover. Microwave for 12 minutes or until cauliflower is tender. Drain and then keep warm.

While cauliflower is microwaving: If using lobster tails, bring 4 cups of water to a boil and then reduce until water is just barely simmering. Add the lobster tails to the water and poach for 7 minutes. Remove the tails from the water to cool slightly. Cut the lobster tails, remove the meat from the tails and chop. Makes about a cup of lobster meat.

Add olive oil to a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes. Add the milk while whisking. Add the nutmeg, salt, pepper and hot sauce. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the Colby-Jack and cream cheeses and stir until melted.
Add the cauliflower to the baking dish. Use a fork to break up the florets into 1-inch or smaller pieces.
Pour the cheese sauce over the cauliflower and stir to coat.
Sprinkle the lobster over the cauliflower and stir to coat.
Sprinkle the panko bread crumbs evenly over the top of the casserole and then spray the top of the panko with cooking spray.
Bake for 30 minutes.

title: Cauliflower "Rice" Salad
description: This low-carb dish pairs nicely with just about everything and takes little time to make too.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 260mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 300mg 6%
steps: Cauliflower "rice" can be purchased frozen at some stores or you can make your own by following this instruction: place cauliflower florets in food processor and process until rice-like consistency (be careful not to over process).
In a large bowl, combine the cauliflower rice, cucumber, tomatoes, green onion, and olives.
In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, oil, and mustard.Pour dressing over salad and toss to combine.
Pour dressing over salad and serve with reduced fat feta cheese if desired.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Cauliflower Tabbouleh
description: Tabbouleh is a traditional mediterranean salad made with flavorful herbs, fresh lemon, and couscous. This diabetes-friendly version uses cauliflower rice for lower carb, grain-free alternative.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 125mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 350mg 7%
ingredients: 1 head small head cauliflower (or 16-oz frozen cauliflower rice) (leaves and stem removed)
steps: Mince the parsley and mint leaves (or grind in a food processor) and add to a large bowl.
Grate the cauliflower using a box grater and stir together with the parsley and mint.
Add the diced tomato and stir it into the salad.
Drizzle the salad with the olive oil and lemon juice, and sprinkle with the salt (optional) and black pepper. Stir to coat.
Cover and let the tabbouleh marinate for 30 minutes before serving.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Cauliflower with Pancetta and Onions
description: Cauliflower is a great nonstarchy vegetable to cook as the holidays come up. Try this savory recipe out, it will pair great with some Roasted Turkey and Vegetables.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 180mg 4%
ingredients: 1 head, about 6 cups (1 1/4lb) cauliflower (trimmed and cut into florets)
steps: Heat 1 Tbsp. of the olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium heat. Add the pancetta and cook until it is crisp. Remove the pancetta with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Add in the onions, and turn the heat to medium low. Sauté the onions for about 8 minutes. Add in the cauliflower, salt, pepper, and bay leaf.

Add in the water, cover and raise the heat to medium. Cook for about 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until the cauliflower is tender and lightly browned. Remove and discard the bay leaf. Add the cauliflower to a serving bowl. Mix together the remaining olive oil and lemon juice, and add to the cauliflower, mixing well. Top with the crisp pancetta.

title: Cheese and Veggie Pitas
description: This vegetarian pita sandwich recipe is easy to make for a crowd. It’s also easy to pack and take to work so you don’t have to eat out at lunch time.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 6g 30%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 260mg 6%
steps: Slice one side of each pita to open pocket, but do not cut all the way through. Set aside.
Spread 1/2 Tbsp of mayonnaise in each pita.
Slice Swiss cheese into 4 even slices. Spread 2 Tbsp of hummus on each cheese slice and sprinkle 1 Tbsp of sunflower seeds on top.
Layer about 1/2 cup of the arugula, onion slices, tomato slices, and cucumber slices on top of hummus.
Stuff each pita with sandwich filling and cut in half.

title: Cheesy Cauliflower Tots
description: Serve these tasty little tots to the family as a side with dinner. Not only are these a much healthier and diabetes-friendly version of classic tater tots, but the flavor is so similar, they may not realize they are eating cauliflower!
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 330mg 7%
ingredients: 2 stalks green onion (scallion) (white and green parts, minced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Coat one large or two small baking sheets with cooking spray. Set aside.
Steam the cauliflower for 10-12 minutes or until soft. Set aside to cool. Once cool, mince the cauliflower.
Stir the remaining ingredients into the minced cauliflower, and let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
After resting, stir the mixture again. Scoop cauliflower with a Tbsp. measure onto the sprayed baking sheet. Form the ball into the shape of a tater-tot. Repeat to make 35 tots.
Spray the top of each tot with cooking spray. Bake for 15 minutes. Turn the tots and bake an additional 10 minutes or until golden brown.
credits: Recipe by: Lare Rondinelli-Hamilton and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough
Photo by: Photography by Terry Doran, Food Styling by Skyler Myers

title: Chicken and Apricot Tagine
description: Serve this dish with whole-wheat couscous or quinoa for a traditional Moroccan meal. For a lower carb meal, serve over spiralized carrots or cauliflower rice.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 21g; Potassium 220mg 5%
ingredients: 5 thighs (about 3 1/2-oz each) boneless, skinless chicken thighs
steps: In a small bowl, combine the cinnamon, ground ginger, turmeric, ground black pepper and salt.
Add oil and a generous amount of cooking spray to a large sauté pan over high heat.
Season both sides of the chicken thighs with the spice mixture.
Sear the chicken on both sides until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.
Add the onion, garlic and apricots and stir into the chicken thighs. Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and the internal temperature is at least 165°F.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Bring the sauce to a low boil for 8-10 minutes or until reduced and slightly thickened.
Add chicken thighs back into the sauce and stir to coat. Stir in the chopped parsley and serve.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chicken and Dumplings
description: Try these chicken and dumplings for a budget-friendly family dinner. Add a side of roasted green beans to complete your meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 26g; Potassium 550mg 12%
ingredients: 8 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, low-sodium)
steps: Mix the flours, baking soda, baking powder, sage, salt (optional), and pepper in a medium bowl. Add yogurt, egg, and water and knead to make a slightly sticky dough. Cover the bowl and set aside.
Add cooking spray and olive oil to a large soup pot over medium high heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery, and mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes or until the vegetables are softened.
Add the chicken and broth, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Roll the dough out into an 8 inch disk that is 1/2-inch thick. Cut the dough into 1 inch pieces and drop the dumplings into the simmering broth. Stir frequently until all the dumplings are added.
Simmer the dumplings for 10 minutes and serve.

title: Chicken and Spinach Enchiladas
description: Trying to eat more veggies? Here’s a great way to incorporate veggies into an everyday dish. Short on time? Use a cooked rotisserie chicken from your local grocery store.
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 23g; Potassium 340mg 7%
ingredients: 9 oz frozen spinach (chopped, thawed and drained)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Spray a large metal or glass baking dish with cooking spray.
In a small bowl, combine spinach, garlic, cumin, cilantro, pepper, and cheddar cheese; mix to incorporate. Add shredded chicken; mix to incorporate.
Scoop 1/4 cup chicken-spinach mixture into a tortilla. Roll tortilla and place seam side down in a baking dish. Repeat process for remaining 11 tortillas.
Pour enchilada sauce over tortillas. Bake 25 minutes.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Soup
description: Soup is a healthy meal that you can load with lots of veggies. If desired, you can add some brown or wild rice to this dish, but add some extra water. This soup would go well with our Orange and Walnut Salad
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 16g; Potassium 380mg 8%
steps: Add the oil to a large soup pot or dutch oven and heat over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and sear for 4 minutes on each side. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add the carrots, celery, and mushrooms to the same pot and sauté over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients and add the chicken back to the pot. Bring to a boil; reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and shred or cut up. Add the chicken back to the pot; stir.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
description: Wild rice is a whole-grain and a healthier option than white rice. This soup is hearty and perfect on a cold winter day.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 2g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 25mg 8%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 13g; Potassium 300mg 6%
ingredients: 1 cup water (+ 1 Tbsp cold water, divided use)
steps: Melt the margarine in a large soup pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 3 minutes or until clear. Add the carrots, celery, and mushrooms, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken broth, water, thyme, black pepper, and salt.
In a small cup, mix together the corn starch and 1 Tbsp. cold water. Add the mixture to the soup.
Bring to a boil and stir in the rice.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes. Add the cooked chicken and stir well.

title: Chicken Cheddar Rice with Asparagus
description: Who doesn’t love chicken and rice? This recipe will be a family favorite. Plus it sneaks in some non-starchy vegetables!
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 43g 16%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 21g; Potassium 360mg 8%
ingredients: 8 oz chicken thigh meat (boneless, skinless, trimmed of fat and cut into bite-size pieces)
1 cup uncooked brown rice (preferably parboiled variety)
2 cup fresh asparagus tips (broken in 2-inch pieces, or frozen French cut green beans, thawed)
steps: Coat a 3 1/2- to 4-quart slow cooker with cooking spray. Place the water, chicken, onion, rice, garlic, chicken bouillon, and thyme in the slow cooker. Cover and cook on high for 1 1/2 hours or on low for 3 hours.
Turn off the heat. Fluff the rice with a fork. Stir in the asparagus. Cover and let stand 10 minutes. Stir in the salt and sprinkle with the cheese.

title: Chicken Joes
description:
OK, so time for a confession. While we always had home-cooked meals, we also always had a can of Sloppy Joe mix tucked into the corner of the pantry for when we got lazy. Knowing now that processed foods are not healthy, I developed these Chicken Joes that are much more diabetes-friendly with all the same taste of the sloppy Joes of childhood. With extra vegetables, this version makes the grade.

To lower the amount of carbs use half a bun to make an open-faced sandwich.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 35mg 12%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 8g; Potassium 370mg 8%
ingredients: 1 med red or green bell pepper (chopped)
steps: In a large skillet, cook the ground chicken, onion, garlic, chili powder, paprika, and pepper over medium heat until meat is browned, about 5–6 minutes.
Add in the green or red pepper and zucchini and cook over low heat for about 5 minutes, until vegetables are tender. Add the diced tomatoes and BBQ sauce and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve the mixture on a toasted bun.

title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps
description: These chicken lettuce wraps are a fresh, easy meal filled with seasoned chicken and crisp vegetables. This is a low-carb recipe because it uses lettuce leaves as wraps instead of bread.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 20mg 7%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 6g; Potassium 110mg 2%
ingredients: 6 leaves lettuce (Boston or Bib lettuce work well)
steps: Mix the green onion, carrots, peanut sauce, and chicken together in a bowl. Divide the mixture evenly among 6 lettuce leaves.

title: Chicken Nacho Casserole
description: This low-fat chicken nacho casserole is a warm, comforting dish made with chicken, beans, vegetables, and bold spices. It has all the flavors of nachos baked into one easy meal. It’s simple to prepare and great for a filling, family‑friendly dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 20g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 25g; Potassium 645mg 14%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into small pieces)
1 (15 ounce) can no-salt-added black beans (drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Spray a 2 ½-quart baking dish with cooking spray.
Season the chicken with black pepper. Spray a large sauté pan with cooking spray and heat over medium-high. Add the chicken and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, black beans, chili powder, cumin, and garlic powder to the pan. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the chicken mixture into the baking dish. Sprinkle on the cheese and then top with the crushed tortilla chips. Bake for 12 minutes or until the cheese is melted.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chicken Salad with Strawberries
description: The strawberries and poppy seed dressing give this 5-ingredient salad a refreshing sweet taste that’s still low in carbohydrate.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 22g; Potassium 580mg 12%
steps: In a salad bowl, mix together all salad ingredients
Pour dressing over salad and toss to coat.

title: Chicken Satay
description: This makes a great party appetizer. You can serve the dip in a bowl on a large platter and surround it with the skewers.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 28g; Potassium 480mg 10%
ingredients: 2 tbsp lower sodium soy sauce (divided use)
1/2 tsp Asian-style hot sauce, such as sriracha
steps: Soak bamboo skewers in warm water for at least 30 minutes. While skewers are soaking, slice chicken breasts into eight strips lengthwise.

In a medium bowl, whisk together 1 tbsp brown sugar substitute, 1 tbsp soy sauce, half the minced garlic, ginger, lime juice and hot sauce. Add chicken to the marinade and marinate chicken strips in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.

While the chicken is marinating, whisk together the remaining tbsp brown sugar substitute, remaining tbsp soy sauce, remaining minced garlic, peanut butter, and coconut milk in a microwave safe bowl. Set aside.
Thread chicken strips lengthwise onto the soaked bamboo skewers. Grill chicken for 4-5 minutes one each side.
Right before serving, microwave sauce for 30 seconds. Remove from microwave and whisk again to combine. Serve two skewers with 2 Tbsps. of sauce.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli-Hamilton, RD, CDE, and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chicken, Mushroom and Barley Soup
description: With our tips for bulk cooking barley in advance, this soup can be a quick and easy weeknight meal. If you’re tight on time, pick up a pre-chopped blend of onion, carrots and celery.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 13g; Potassium 430mg 9%
steps: Add oil to a soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Add broth, thyme, bay leaves, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer, covered for 20 minutes.
Remove bay leaves and thyme stem. Add the barley and chicken and heat through for 2-3 minutes.

Note: To bulk cook barley, add 11 oz. dry pearled (quick-cooking) barley to a pot of 4 cups boiling water. Cover, then reduce to a simmer for 10-12 minutes. Remove from heat, keep covered off the heat for 5 minutes. Makes 6 cups cooked barley. This barley can be used in any recipe calling for cooked barley. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 7 days or package in freezer bags in one cup increments for up to 6 months.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Chickpea Tabbouleh
description: Bulgur is the grain used in traditional tabbouleh, but the bulk of this tasty tabbouleh is made up of vegetables, herbs and protein-packed chickpeas.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 130mg 6%; Total Carbohydrate 14g 5%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 290mg 6%
ingredients: 1 cup hot water (to cover and soak bulgur)
1/2 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced (about 1/2 cup))
steps: Rinse the bulgur wheat and add it to a small bowl. Pour hot water over the bulgur, cover, and let soak for about 20 minutes, until doubled in size. Drain excess liquid, if any, and place the bulgur in a large bowl.

Chop the parsley to a medium-fine consistency. It should have some texture left in it and should not look pureed. Add the parsley to the bulgur wheat, and add all the remaining salad ingredients. Cover and set aside.

For the vinaigrette, in a small bowl, whisk together the ingredients. Add to the salad; taste and adjust any seasonings. Add more lemon juice if desired. Turn the tabbouleh out onto a platter to serve.

title: Chili Lime Corn on the Cob
description: Nothing says summer like corn on the cob. It’s an American favorite and this recipe puts a nice twist of flavor into it. Remember, corn is a starchy vegetable, so serve it with some lean protein and a low-carb vegetable like green beans, zucchini or a salad.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 85mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 280mg 6%
steps: Preheat the grill to medium-high.
In a small bowl, mix together the lime juice, lime zest, margarine, and chili powder.
Using a spoon and your hands, spread the margarine mixture evenly over the 4 ears of corn.
Wrap the corn individually in aluminum foil. Grill 20 minutes, turning frequently. Serve hot.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chinese Five-Spice Kale Chips
description: Chinese five-spice powder is a mixture of five spices: star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and fennel. It gives a sweet, salty, sour, bitter and pungent taste to dishes. Don’t have it? Try a simplified Asian three-spice powder: mix equal parts ground cloves, ginger, and cinnamon. Either mix is perfect for this kale chip side dish, that's a nutrition powerhouse and packed with flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 390mg 8%
ingredients: 1 bunch kale (stems and tough ribs removed, cut into large bite-size pieces (5 packed pieces))
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F. Add the kale to a large bowl and toss well with the oil, five-spice powder and salt.
Arrange the leaves in a single layer onto 2 large baking sheets. Bake until the leaves are crisp, about 20 minutes.
Transfer the sheets to racks to cool, then serve.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Chipotle Chili and Tea Rubbed Salmon
description: Spice rubs are simple to make and keep in the refrigerator for weeks. Try this rub on seafood, meat, poultry, or vegetables.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 23g; Potassium 564mg 12%
ingredients: 1 tbsp ground tea leaves (green or black)
steps: Place all ingredients except the salmon in a blender or food processor and purée until smooth.
Rub the mixture over the surface of the salmon. Place the salmon on a baking dish and let marinate for 20 minutes.

Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. You can cook the salmon directly on a piece of foil or place them on a perforated grill grate used for fish or vegetables. Cook over indirect heat (away from the heat source) for 5–6 minutes on each side. The salmon is done when it reads 145 degrees F on an instant thermometer.
Cool for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Chia Seed Pudding
description: This pudding is decadent enough to be a fancy dessert for two, or light enough for breakfast or a midday snack. Chia seeds are a diabetes superfood. They are high in fiber and omega-3 fatty acids—great for blood glucose (blood sugar) management and heart health. When combined with liquid, they form a gel creating a pudding-like texture. To make this vegan, use a non-dairy milk like almond or soy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 95mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 24g 9%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 10g; Potassium 350mg 7%
ingredients: 1 cup skim milk or unsweetened almond milk
steps: Mix cocoa powder, low- or no-calorie sweetener, and powdered peanut butter together, and incorporate well so there are no lumps.
Stir in the chia seeds and stir well to combine.
Whisk in the milk and vanilla. Let sit for 5 minutes, then whisk again. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Chocolate Walnut Mug Cake
description: When you want dessert, this cake that’s made inside a coffee mug is a great way to enjoy a portion-controlled treat.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 13g 17%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 320mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 220mg 5%
steps: Spray a coffee mug with cooking spray.
Add the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, salt, stevia, canola oil, milk and vanilla and stir to combine.
Microwave for 45 seconds.
Top with the walnuts and serve.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Chopped Black Bean Chicken Salad
description: You can either use leftover chicken breasts for this quick and easy recipe or purchase a cooked rotisserie chicken from your local grocery store.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 19g; Potassium 440mg 9%
ingredients: 1/2 cup canned black beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: In a large salad bowl, add all of the ingredients, except salad dressing, and toss.
Add the salad dressing and toss to coat well. Divide evenly among 5 bowls.

title: Chopped Salad with Cilantro Lime Dressing
description: Instead of a tossed salad, try something new and different. Rows of salad ingredients make for a pretty presentation and it’s easy to identify exactly what you’re eating. The cilantro dressing is so sublime; pour it over any other green salad to make that salad shine.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 190mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 2g; Potassium 290mg 6%
steps: Place the lettuce on a shallow platter. In rows, arrange the carrots, celery, plum tomatoes, cucumber, and black beans.
Prepare the salad dressing. Whisk together the cider vinegar, lime juice, cilantro, honey, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in the oil, whisking to incorporate.
Drizzle on the dressing. Top with toasted pumpkin or sunflower seeds.

title: Cilantro Lime Quinoa
description: Quinoa has more protein than any other grain. It is gluten-free, contains 2 grams fiber per serving, and is a healthy alternative to any recipe that uses rice.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 40mg 2%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 200mg 4%
ingredients: 2 cup low sodium vegetable broth (fat-free, (gluten-free if needed))
4 tbsp fresh lime juice (from 2 med limes)
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Reduce the heat to low and add quinoa. Cook over a low heat for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly to make sure the quinoa doesn’t burn.
Add the vegetable broth and the juice of 1 lime and bring it to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes or until done. Remove from heat.
Stir in the juice of 1 lime and chopped cilantro.

title: Cinnamon Ginger Apple On A Stick
description: A novel approach to dessert. The crushed nuts add crunch and eye appeal. You can also cut the apples in quarters and place a few different varieties on each stick.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 1g; Potassium 130mg 3%
ingredients: 3 apple ((Granny Smith, Fuji, Rome, or Gala), peeled, halved, and core removed)
steps: Place the apple halves, lemon juice, ginger, cinnamon and honey in a resealable bag and seal it shut. Turn the bag to coat the apples with the mixture and allow the apples to marinate for 30 minutes.

Preheat grill to medium high. Remove the apples from the bag and place on the grill. Cook for 5–6 minutes, turning once until they are golden brown on the outside and just warmed through on the inside.
Remove apples from the grill, cool for a few minutes, and roll in crushed walnuts. Press gently.
Place a skewer in each apple half and serve.

title: Cinnamon Maple Grilled Peaches
description: Who said desserts can’t be grilled? Try dressing up this simple dish by garnishing it with some fresh mint leaves.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 15g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 1g; Potassium 310mg 7%
ingredients: 4 peaches or nectarines (still firm but ripe)
steps: Cut peaches in half and remove the seed. Place peach halves in a resealable plastic bag.
Mix the lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and maple syrup in a small bowl. Pour the mixture over the peaches in the bag. Seal the bag and turn to coat the peaches.
Preheat grill to medium high. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until golden brown on the outside, and just warmed through inside.

title: Cinnamon Roasted Pears
description: Fruit is a great end to a meal. By experimenting with roasting and grilling fruit, you can bring out its maximum flavor. This recipe could easily be made with apples too.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 25mg 1%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 110mg 2%
ingredients: 2 medium Anjou Pears ((about 6.5 ounces each) peeled, cored and sliced in half)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a small bowl (using fingers) combine margarine, cinnamon and brown sugar. Add walnuts and mix.
Arrange the pears cut side up in an 8-inch square glass baking dish. Pour 1/4 cup water in bottom of pan.
Divide the brown sugar mixture evenly among the pear halves and place in middle of pears.
Bake until the pears are tender and beginning to brown, about 45 minutes.

title: Citrus Grilled Shrimp with Spring Greens
description: A light and easy dish, this grilled shrimp offers a lot of flavors. It can be eaten on its own or with a side of a nonstarchy dish like cauliflower rice.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 35mg 12%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 390mg 8%
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together orange and lime juice, hot sauce, garlic and pepper. Add shrimp to bowl and place in refrigerator to marinate for 20 minutes.
Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill to medium. Spray grill rack with cooking spray.
Place shrimp on skewers and grill for 2-3 minutes on each side or until shrimp are done.
Serve shrimp on top of spring mix salad with clementine slices.
Whisk together dressing ingredients and pour over shrimp and salad.
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Citrus Mahi-Mahi Packet with Broccoli
description: If you’re not sure how to start cooking fish, try a simple and delicious method like this packet. It’s full of fresh flavors from lemon, orange and dill. Sealing the fish in a parchment paper pouch steams it to perfection and infuses the fish with flavor from the citrus and herbs. If you don't have parchment paper, aluminum foil will also work. We used mahi-mahi, but you could make this recipe with any type of fish filet.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 105mg 35%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 32g; Potassium 1260mg 27%
steps: Preheat oven to 425° F. Place two pieces parchment paper on a baking sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and dill.

Place a few lemon and orange slices on center of parchment papers. Place fish fillets on top of orange and lemon slices. Drizzle lemon sauce evenly over fish fillets. Top fish with remaining orange and lemon slices. Fold over the top of the parchment paper, then roll the sides in to form a sealed pouch.
Place packets on baking sheet and bake for 25 minutes or until done.
While fish is baking, steam broccoli for 5-6 minutes.
Serve fish packet with steamed broccoli. Be cautious when opening fish packet, as steam may be hot.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Classic Beef Stew
description: You don’t need cold weather to enjoy a great beef stew. There are so many new renditions of beef stew, but if you can make this classic version really well, that’s all you’ll need. Although button mushrooms can be used, try and seek out cremini mushrooms as the stew will taste more full-bodied.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 135mg 6%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 26g; Potassium 880mg 19%
ingredients: 2 tbsp all-purpose flour or whole-wheat pastry flour
1 1/2 lbs cremini (baby bella) mushrooms (cleaned, stemmed, and quartered)
4 cup low sodium chicken broth (reduced-sodium, low-fat, divided use)
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper (1/4-1/2 tsp)
steps: Combine the all-purpose flour with the Italian seasoning. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Dredge the beef cubes lightly in the flour mixture and add the beef, in batches to keep the beef in one layer, until well browned on each side.

Remove the beef from the pan and deglaze the pan with 1/4 cup chicken broth. Add in the mushrooms and sauté for about 4 minutes until well browned. Remove the mushrooms from the pan and deglaze with another 1/4 cup of the broth. Add the onions and garlic and sauté for 4 minutes. Return the beef to the pot, add the remaining chicken broth, and bring to a boil. Partially cover, lower the heat to simmer, and cook for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Peel and cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch pieces. Cut the carrots into 1/2-inch pieces. Add the potatoes and carrots to the stew and continue to cook for another 45 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Add in the reserved mushrooms, peas, and thyme. Season with red wine vinegar and black pepper.

title: Classic Italian Panzanella Salad
description: This classic bread and tomato salad pairs well with any roasted meat or poultry entrée. Double the recipe and it can also make a great side dish at your holiday feast this year!
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 4g; Potassium 420mg 9%
ingredients: 2 medium tomatoes (cut into 1-inch cubes (or 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved))
1 cup cucumber(s) (quartered lengthwise and thinly sliced (about 1/2 an English cucumber))
1 small red onion (cut in half and thinly sliced)
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves (torn into strips)
1 cup flat Italian parsley leaves (roughly chopped)
steps: Place tomatoes in large salad bowl and sprinkle with salt. Let stand 5 minutes.
Break up bread and add to tomatoes. Add remaining salad ingredients and mix well.

title: Ratatouille
description: This is another great side dish for the holidays. It’s packed with vegetables and is relatively low in calories.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 480mg 10%
steps: Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add garlic and sauté 30 seconds.
Add remaining ingredients and cook 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender.

title: Coconut Curry Trail Mix
description: This quick and satisfying snack is great when you need something to take with you that wont spoil. You can portion out 2 Tbsp. servings in snack-size containers to help with portion control.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 4g; Potassium 120mg 3%
steps: In a medium plastic container place almonds, peanuts, chocolate chips, sunflower seeds and coconut. Spray mixture evenly with cooking spray and then sprinkle on curry powder. Place lid on plastic container and gently shake contents to mix well.

title: Cod on Roasted Pepper and White Beans
description: This dish calls for fish and beans – both tasty, lean protein options! Serve it with a green salad or steamed green beans to round out your meal.
serving_size: 1, 5 oz fish fillet and 1 cup tomato, pepper, and bean mixture
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 30g; Potassium 950mg 20%
ingredients: 4 whole fish fillets (such as cod, about 5 ounces each, patted dry)
3 tsp Extra Virgin Olive Oil (divided use)
1 can, 14.5 oz canned diced tomatoes, no salt added
1 can, 15 ounces canned navy or great northern beans (no-salt-added, rinsed and drained)
1/2 tsp fresh (1 tsp dried) fresh rosemary or to taste (chopped)
steps: In a small bowl, combine the paprika, 1/4 Tsp. of salt, and black pepper. Sprinkle both sides of the fillets with the paprika mixture. Heat 1 Tsp. of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the fillets 4 minutes, turn, and cook 3 minutes or until opaque in center.

Place tomatoes in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat to just boiling. Add the beans, red peppers, garlic, 2 tsp olive oil and rosemary and cook 1-2 minutes to heat through. Remove from heat, cover, and let stand while fish is cooking.
Divide the tomato, bean and pepper mixture equally between 4 shallow bowls and top each with a fish fillet.

title: Congrí Light (Cuban Black Beans and Rice)
description: This healthy and classic Cuban recipe is a great dish to bring to parties or add on as a side to make a complete meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 2g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 500mg 11%
ingredients: 10 oz black beans (dried, sorted and rinsed (1 1/2 cups))
steps: Into a stovetop pressure cooker, add rinsed beans and 3 cups water, and cover. Place pressure cooker on stove and set on high heat. Once the beans start boiling, lower heat to medium and cook beans until they are tender, about 45 minutes. Make sure beans submerged in water while they cook; add more water if needed.
Once beans are tender, add rice, 1 cup water, salt and 1/2 Tsp. avocado oil. Stir well and add the remaining ingredients. Stir once more with spoon, and make sure to put a little hip into it.

Make sure there is about 3/4 inch of water above the beans. Cover the mixture, and put heat on medium-low. Cook for 15 minutes, or until rice is tender. Once the congrí is done, fluff with a fork and serve. Enjoy!
credits: Recipe by: Jen Bucko and Lara Hamilton

title: Corn, Tomato, Pea and Dill Salad
description: Get ready for summer with this crisp and colorful salad. Serve it alongside roasted turkey or grilled fish for a well-balanced and satisfying meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 320mg 7%
ingredients: 1 tsp Freshly ground pepper, to taste
1 cup sugar snap peas or English peas
steps: Place peas in a saucepan, and cover with water. Bring to a boil over high heat, and cook for 5 minutes or until tender. Drain. Rinse with cold water.
Combine peas, corn, tomatoes, olive oil, dill, basil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Toss well to combine. Serve at room temperature.

title: Cowboy Bean Fritters
description: Bring this appetizer to share at your next summer barbeque. Serve the fritters with some dipping options like salsa and non-fat plain Greek yogurt (a healthier substitute for sour cream).
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 1g 1%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 14g 5%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 160mg 3%
ingredients: 2 can black beans (16-ounce, rinsed and drained)
1 tbsp vegetable oil (plus extra if needed)
steps: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add egg whites and salsa; mix well, then stir in black beans.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 Tbsp. oil. Pour 1 Tsp. batter per fritter into skillet, cooking several fritters at one time, but not overcrowding them. Cook 1 minute, then turn fritters and lightly flatten with a spatula; cook 1 to 2 additional minutes or until browned on both sides. Repeat with remaining batter, adding more oil as necessary.

title: Crab Cake Burger
