Place the seasoned green beans on the preheated grill. Grill for 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, or until the beans are tender and have grill marks.
While the green beans are grilling, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, and 2 Tbsp chopped fresh basil. Add tomatoes to the dressing.
Once the green beans are done, transfer them to a serving platter.
Pour dressing and tomatoes over the green bean salad.
Top with the crumbled blue cheese and remaining basil leaves.

title: Grilled Lime Chicken Salad Lettuce Wraps
description: Fresh, crunchy, and delicious, these Grilled Lime Chicken Salad Lettuce Wraps are an excellent lunch choice for people with diabetes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 100mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 24g; Potassium 346mg 7%
ingredients: 12 leaves lettuce leaves (large, such as butter or iceberg)
steps: In a bowl, combine the lime zest, lime juice, olive oil, minced garlic, ground cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper to make the marinade.
Place the chicken breasts in a sealable bag or shallow dish and pour half of the marinade over the chicken. Toss to fully coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill or a grill pan over medium high heat.
Grill the marinated chicken breasts for about 6–8 minutes per side or until fully cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degreed F.
Allow the chicken to rest for a few minutes before slicing it into strips.
In a bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and fresh cilantro.
Pour the remaining marinade over the vegetable mixture and toss gently.
Place two lettuce leaves on each plate.
Top with the vegetable salad mixture.

title: Grilled Zucchini Bites with Tomato, Olive, and Pinenut Salsa
description: Amp up your grilled zucchini with this diabetes-friendly recipe. A fresh salsa made of tomatoes, olives, and pine nuts adds a savory kick to low-carb zucchini.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 172mg 4%
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the tomato, kalamata olives, pine nuts, parsley, and ¼ tsp kosher salt. Set aside.
Preheat a grill pan or grill over medium high heat.
In a bowl, toss zucchini slices with coconut oil, minced garlic, and ¼ tsp kosher salt. Place on grill and grill 3 minutes per side.
Serve each slice warm with a generous topping of the salsa.

title: Grilled Zucchini
description: This grilled zucchini is a quick side dish that is simple, fresh, and full of flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 256mg 5%
steps: Preheat the grill or a grill pan to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, toss the zucchini rounds with olive oil, dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Use tongs to place the rounds on the grill.
Grill for 3–4 minutes on each side, until tender and charred in places.

title: Mashed Butternut Squash
description: Great for a fall or winter side dish, this diabetes-friendly Mashed Butternut Squash is a delicious and low-carb alternative to mashed potatoes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 677mg 14%
steps: Steam or boil the butternut squash cubes until the cubes are fork-tender. If steamed, remove the cooked squash from the steamer basket and pour it into a large bowl. If boiled, strain the butternut squash and then add to a large bowl.
Add the minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper and mash until smooth.

title: Mashed Turnips
description: Try our vibrant Mashed Turnips recipe for a low-calorie delight bursting with vitamins and antioxidants, perfect for a nutrient-packed side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 217mg 5%
steps: Add water to a large saucepan and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the cubed turnips and boil until tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain and then return the turnips to the pot.
Add butter, minced garlic, and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Mediterranean Baked Eggplant
description: Nutrient-rich eggplant gets a Mediterranean-inspired makeover in this easy side dish recipe. Fresh tomatoes, crumbled feta, and herbs take this diabetes-friendly dish to the next level of deliciousness.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 421mg 9%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Lay the eggplant rounds on a baking sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Brush both sides of each eggplant round with the olive oil mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then flip the eggplant rounds and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until they are tender and golden brown.
Remove the eggplant from the oven.
Sprinkle halved cherry tomatoes and crumbled feta cheese over the baked eggplant.
Return the baking sheet to the oven and bake for an additional 5 minutes, or until the feta is softened and tomatoes are slightly roasted.

title: Baked Egg and Zoodle Bundle
description: These baked zoodle bundles are a fresh, veggie-forward way to enjoy eggs with a burst of pesto flavor and creamy Greek yogurt. The higher protein and fiber content can help support steady energy throughout the morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 190mg 63%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 361mg 8%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Lightly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
In a small bowl, mix yogurt and pesto.
Toss the zucchini noodles with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
On the prepared baking sheet, create 4 small nests with zucchini. Evenly distribute tomato halves among them.
Bake for 5 minutes until slightly softened. Remove from the oven. Create a small well in the center of each nest. Spoon pesto yogurt mixture into each well. Crack 1 egg into each well.
Return to the oven and bake for 10-12 minutes, until eggs reach desired doneness.
Remove from the oven, sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese and fresh basil. Serve immediately.

title: Cheesy Broccoli Spaghetti Squash Bake
description: This cheesy broccoli spaghetti squash bake is a comforting, lower-carb alternative to traditional casseroles, with plenty of fiber and flavor packed into every bite.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 430mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 528mg 11%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Cut squash in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds. Drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet and roast until fork-tender, about 35-40 minutes. Let cool slightly, then use a fork to shred into strands.
While squash is roasting, bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add broccoli and cook until just tender, about 3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and cook garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in broth, milk, Dijon mustard, and paprika. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and stir in cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
To prevent curdling, remove sauce from heat before adding Greek yogurt. Temper by mixing 1-2 Tbsp of warm sauce into the yogurt first, then slowly stir into the pan.

In a large mixing bowl, combine spaghetti squash, broccoli, and cheese sauce. Transfer to a baking dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and slightly golden.

title: Cheesy Tomato and White Bean "Pizza" Skillet
description: This “pizza” skillet combines the comfort of a cheesy tomato bake with the wholesomeness of white beans and spinach for a satisfying one-pan meal. It’s rich in plant-based protein and fiber, which can help promote stable blood sugar (blood glucose) levels.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 720mg 15%
ingredients: 1 1/2 cup canned crushed tomatoes (no added salt)
1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans (no added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to broil.

Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, oregano, and red pepper flakes, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth, then season with the salt and black pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the white beans and spinach, cooking for another 3-4 minutes until the spinach wilts and the beans are heated through.
Sprinkle the mozzarella and Parmesan evenly over the skillet. Place the skillet in the oven and broil until the cheese is melted and golden-brown, 2-3 minutes.
Remove from the oven and garnish with fresh basil.

title: Chickpea Salad with Creamy Tahini Dressing
description: This crisp and refreshing chickpea salad is tossed with a creamy homemade tahini dressing for a simple, plant-based meal that’s big on flavor and fiber. Chickpeas provide satisfying protein and slow-digesting carbs that can help support stable blood glucose (blood sugar). It’s a nourishing, no-cook option that’s especially well-suited for those looking for a fresh, filling lunch.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 10g 36%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 640mg 14%
ingredients: 1 cup canned chickpeas (no added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the tahini, fresh lemon juice, crushed garlic, and salt.​ Gradually add cold water, whisking continuously until the dressing reaches a smooth, pourable consistency.​
In a separate large bowl, combine the chopped romaine lettuce, cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, and chickpeas.​ Add sliced red onion and chopped parsley. Drizzle the tahini dressing over the salad.​

title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Spinach
description: This Tuscan chicken has creamy comfort without the heavy cream, thanks to a mix of low-fat milk and Greek yogurt. With lean protein, fiber-rich spinach, and no added sugars, it’s a balanced dish that will help you reach your blood glucose (blood sugar) goals. It’s a great choice if you’re looking for something hearty, flavorful, and diabetes friendly.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 32g; Potassium 599mg 13%
ingredients: 12 oz low sodium chicken broth (fat free)
1/2 cup fresh basil (torn, plus more for serving)
steps: Sprinkle the chicken breasts with the pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken and sear until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 4–5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

In the same skillet, add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in the milk, sun-dried tomatoes, and red pepper flakes. Simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and Parmesan cheese, cooking until spinach wilts, about 1–2 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat once the sauce is finished simmering. In a small bowl, mix ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt with 1–2 Tbsp of the warm sauce to temper it. Slowly stir the tempered yogurt into the pan, mixing gently until fully incorporated.
Return the chicken to the pan. Spoon the sauce over the top. Add half of the basil and simmer for 1–2 minutes to heat through.
Serve with additional fresh basil on top.

title: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette
description: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette is a refreshing and elegant salad that combines the sweetness of ripe melon with the herby and slightly peppery notes of tarragon in a light vinaigrette. It makes for a great low-carb side dish in the summer.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 11g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 275mg 6%
steps: In a small bowl, whisk lemon juice, syrup, chopped tarragon, and oil.
Arrange cantaloupe on a platter, drizzle generously with dressing, and finish with a sprinkling of salt.

title: Low Carb Sushi Bowl
description: This low-carb sushi bowl is a fresh take on takeout, swapping traditional rice for seasoned cauliflower to keep the carbs down without losing flavor. Shrimp adds lean protein, while avocado and veggies bring satisfying texture and healthy fats. It’s a diabetes-friendly option that supports blood glucose (blood sugar) levels without sacrificing any flavor.
serving_size: 3 oz cauliflower rice + 2 oz shrimp + 1 cup veggies + 1 Tbsp mayo
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 16g; Potassium 426mg 9%
steps: Cook the frozen cauliflower rice according to package instructions. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the vinegar, sesame oil, and salt. Let it cool to room temp.
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, sriracha, and lime juice. Set aside.
To assemble, divide the cauliflower rice among 4 bowls. Top each bowl with the diced shrimp, avocado, cucumber, radishes, and green onions.
Drizzle the spicy mayo over each bowl and top with sesame seeds.

title: Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers
description: These Philly Cheesesteak-Stuffed Peppers have all the savory flavors of the original—but without the roll. Swapping the bread for bell peppers helps cut back on carbs while adding fiber and nutrients. It's a great lower carb dinner that can help support steady blood glucose (blood sugar).
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 594mg 13%
ingredients: 2 whole green bell pepper (halved lengthwise, seeds removed)
12 oz top round steak (trimmed of fat, thinly sliced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Arrange the bell pepper halves on a baking sheet with the cut sides facing up. Bake for about 30 minutes or until they are tender but still firm enough to hold their shape.

While the peppers are in the oven, warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and cook for about 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they soften and start to brown.
Stir in the mushrooms and continue cooking for another 5 minutes, allowing them to release their moisture.
Add the steak slices to the pan, along with the Italian seasoning, black pepper, and salt. Cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the steak is browned and cooked through.
Pour in the Worcestershire sauce, stir to combine, and remove the skillet from the heat.
Switch the oven to broil.
Fill each bell pepper half with an equal portion of the steak mixture and sprinkle with cheese.
Return the peppers to the oven and broil for 2–3 minutes, or until the cheese is fully melted and slightly golden.
Top with the chopped green onion to serve.

title: Rotini Caesar Salad with Garlic Croutons
description: This lighter take on Caesar salad blends creamy Greek yogurt dressing with whole grain pasta and crisp romaine for a satisfying, fiber-rich dish. Homemade garlic croutons and shaved Parmesan add crunch and flavor. With smart ingredient swaps and portioned pasta, it’s a balanced, diabetes-friendly spin on a classic favorite.
serving_size: 1 oz pasta + 1/4 cup croutons + 2 cup salad
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 36g 13%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 601mg 13%
ingredients: 2 slice whole grain Ezekiel 4:9 bread (cut into small cubes)
4 oz roasted red peppers (sliced into strips)
4 oz whole wheat penne pasta (cooked and cooled)
steps: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the bread cubes, then sprinkle with dried oregano and garlic powder. Toast the cubes, stirring frequently, until they are golden brown and crisp, about 4-5 minutes. Remove from the skillet and let them cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp olive oil, and black pepper until smooth and well combined.
In a large bowl, toss the chopped romaine lettuce and peppers with the dressing, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
Gently mix the cooked pasta into the salad. Add the toasted croutons and toss lightly to combine.
Divide into 4 servings and top with shaved Parmesan cheese.

title: Smoked Salmon and Greek Yogurt Omelet
description: This elegant omelet pairs silky smoked salmon with creamy Greek yogurt and fresh dill for a protein-rich, satisfying start to the day. It’s a smart breakfast option for those watching their blood glucose (blood sugar), thanks to its low carbohydrate content and balanced protein.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 210mg 70%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 242mg 5%
ingredients: 2 oz cold smoked salmon (low sodium, chopped)
1 tbsp fresh dill (chopped, plus more for garnish)
steps: In a bowl, whisk the eggs, egg whites, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour ¼ of the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook until the edges start to set, about 2 minutes.
Add ¼ of the smoked salmon, a dollop of Greek yogurt, fresh dill, and red onion to one side of the omelet.
Carefully fold the omelet over the filling and cook for 30 seconds to warm through.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining ingredients.

title: Smoky Beef Burger on a Mushroom Bun
description: This burger stacks smoky beef, melted cheddar, and grilled veggies on a savory portobello mushroom “bun” for a low-carb alternative to the classic. Grated zucchini keeps the patties juicy while adding a sneaky dose of veggies.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 31g; Potassium 961mg 20%
ingredients: 1 small zucchini (grated, squeezed to remove excess moisture)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, smoked paprika, grated zucchini, and 1 tablespoon of the barbecue sauce. Mix thoroughly using clean hands, then shape the mixture into four patties, each about ¾-inch thick.

Preheat a large grill pan over medium-high heat. Lightly brush the patties and portobello mushrooms with olive oil. Place the mushrooms on the grill and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until they are tender and have light char marks.

Cook the beef patties for about 4 minutes on the first side until lightly charred. Flip the patties, cook for an additional 2 minutes, then top each with a slice of cheddar cheese. Continue cooking for another 2 minutes until the cheese melts and the patties are cooked through.
Grill the red onion rings for about 2 minutes on each side until they are lightly charred.

To serve, place each grilled mushroom cap on a plate, gill side up. Top with arugula, a slice of tomato, a beef patty with melted cheese, and some grilled onion rings. Drizzle with the remaining barbecue sauce.

title: Southwest Shredded Pork Salad
description: This Southwest-inspired salad layers tender shredded pork with crisp greens, colorful veggies, and a tangy Greek yogurt dressing. It’s high in protein and fiber, with smart seasoning swaps.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 75mg 25%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 30g; Potassium 940mg 20%
ingredients: 1/2 cup black beans (canned, low sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a small bowl, combine the cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, onion powder, and 1/4 tsp pepper. Rub this spice mixture evenly over the pork tenderloin.​
Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork and sear on all sides until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side.​
Transfer the pork to a slow cooker and add the low-sodium chicken broth. Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours, or until the pork is tender and shreds easily with a fork.​
Once cooked, remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Set aside.​

In a small bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lime juice, remaining 2 tsp olive oil, remaining 1/4 tsp chili powder, remaining 1/4 tsp garlic powder, salt, and remaining 1/8 tsp pepper until smooth.
Divide the mixed salad greens among four plates or bowls.​
Top each with equal portions of cherry tomatoes, cucumber, black beans, corn, and red onion.​
Add a portion of the shredded pork to each salad.​
Drizzle the dressing over each salad and gently toss to combine.​ Garnish with fresh cilantro.

title: Orange and Avocado Salad
description: Bright orange and creamy avocado come together in this unique, diabetes-friendly salad. Perfect as a side dish, pair it with a lean protein like grilled chicken breasts for a quick and easy meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 125mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 439mg 9%
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together extra-virgin olive oil, lime juice, unsweetened multi-use syrup, salt, and black pepper.
Arrange oranges, avocados, red onion, and fresh mint on a platter.
Pour the dressing over the salad and top with toasted slivered almonds.

title: Miso Chopped Salad
description: The crunch of cabbage, carrots, and onion pair with an Asian infusion dressing that is diabetes-friendly and would go great with a stir fry dinner!
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 3g; Potassium 338mg 7%
ingredients: 2 stalks scallions (chopped, white and light green parts)
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the soy sauce, white rice miso paste, rice wine vinegar, toasted sesame oil, olive oil, unsweetened multi-use syrup, fresh ginger, and lime juice in a small bowl.
Add in the cabbage, red onion, corn, carrot, scallions, and cilantro and toss to combine.
Allow to rest at least 15 minutes before serving so flavors can meld.

title: Parmesan Roasted Cauliflower
description: Upgrade your roasted cauliflower with some creamy parmesan cheese. This Italian-inspired recipe is a great low carb option to add to your dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 434mg 9%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
In a large bowl, toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, grated Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper until well coated.
Spread the cauliflower in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the cauliflower is golden brown and crispy, tossing halfway through.
Remove the cauliflower from the oven.
Transfer the cauliflower to a serving dish.
Serve the cauliflower as a savory and diabetes-friendly side dish.

title: Perfect Sautéed Carrots
description: It may be bold, but we think these are the perfect way to sauté carrots! Slightly caramelizing the carrots adds a delectable richness and sweetness to this simple recipe and is sure to be a hit with the whole family.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 364mg 8%
ingredients: 1 lbs carrots (peeled and cut into 2–3-inch sticks)
steps: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add the carrots to the skillet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Sauté the carrots for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Season the carrots with the salt, thyme and black pepper.

title: Quick and Easy Sautéed Collard Greens
description: Experience the swift and effortless preparation of sautéed collard greens, where vibrant greens are delicately cooked to perfection, offering a quick and easy side dish that's both nutritious and flavorful.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 187mg 4%
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens (stems removed and leaves chopped)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, if using, to the skillet. Sauté for 1–2 minutes until the garlic becomes fragrant.
Add the collard greens to the skillet. Toss to coat in the garlic and oil.
Sauté the collard greens for 5–7 minutes, or until they are wilted and tender.
Season with the salt and black pepper.
Drizzle apple cider vinegar over the collard greens. Toss to combine.
Continue cooking for an additional 2–3 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

title: Roasted Asparagus and Tomatoes
description: This delightful recipe is all about the simplicity of roasted asparagus and tomatoes, where the tender crunch of asparagus meets the burst of sweetness from roasted tomatoes, creating a diabetes-friendly, vitamin-rich medley.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 336mg 7%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F and cover a sheet pan in parchment paper.
Toss asparagus and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Spread evenly on the sheet pan and roast for 15–20 minutes until asparagus is tender and tomatoes are slightly caramelized.
Platter and garnish with fresh basil.

title: Roasted Beets with Blue Cheese and Hazelnuts
description: This gourmet dish not only showcases vibrant colors, but also adds a sophisticated touch to your diabetes-conscious dining, creating a delightful balance of textures and tastes in every delectable bite.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 340mg 7%
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish, optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, toss the diced beets with olive oil, salt, and black pepper until well coated.
Spread the beets in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 45 minutes or until the beets are tender, stirring halfway through.
Remove the beets from the oven and transfer them to a serving dish.
Sprinkle crumbled blue cheese and toasted hazelnuts over the roasted beets.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Roasted Broccolini with Lemon and Parmesan
description: Experience the perfect balance of flavors in our roasted broccolini with zesty lemon and parmesan in this diabetes-friendly side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 357mg 8%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Zest and juice one lemon.

In a large bowl, toss broccolini with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, grated Parmesan cheese, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Ensure the broccolini is evenly coated.
Spread the broccolini in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes or until the broccolini is tender-crisp and the edges are slightly charred.
Serve with additional grated Parmesan on top. Slice the remaining lemon into wedges to serve on the side if desired.

title: Roasted Carrots with Crispy Bacon

Gradually whisk in vegetable broth and milk to the skillet, ensuring no lumps form.
Add minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Stir continuously until the sauce thickens.

description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. This Salmon and Roasted Vegetable version highlights omega-3 fatty acids and an Asian-inspired flavor.

nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 340mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 36g; Potassium 908mg 19%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix the olive oil, chili sauce, ginger, and lower sodium soy sauce.
Place salmon filets in the center of the sheet pan and brush liberally with the sauce.
Stir the vegetables into the remaining sauce and place on the sheet pan around the salmon.
Roast in the preheated oven for approximately 20 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through to 145 degrees F and the vegetables are tender.
Garnish with a squeeze of fresh lime juice if desired.

title: Smashed Spicy Broccoli
description: The unique smashing technique brings out broccoli’s natural textures, providing a delightful and nutrient-packed twist to this spicy side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 180mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 402mg 9%
steps: Steam the broccoli florets until they are just tender, about 5 minutes. Alternatively, blanch them in boiling water for 3–4 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the red pepper flakes and minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1–2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant.
Add the steamed broccoli to the skillet.
Using a fork or potato masher, gently smash the broccoli, allowing it to absorb the flavors of the garlic and red pepper flakes.
Continue cooking for an additional 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the broccoli edges are crispy and golden brown.
Zest the lemon over the smashed broccoli and squeeze the lemon juice on top.
Season with the salt and black pepper. Toss to combine.

title: Spinach and Red Onion Salad with Lemon Poppyseed Dressing
description: Enjoy a burst of freshness with our Spinach and Red Onion Salad paired with a zesty Lemon Poppyseed Dressing. Tossed together, this salad invites you to savor the delightful combination of textures and flavors, creating a refreshing addition to your meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 188mg 4%
steps: In a large salad bowl, combine fresh baby spinach, thinly sliced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, toasted sliced almonds, and dried cranberries.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, fresh lemon juice, Dijon mustard, honey, poppy seeds, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Toss gently to ensure even coating.
Allow the salad to sit for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.

title: Steamed Broccoli with Crispy Garlic
description: Crispy garlic adds a deliciously modern twist to simple steamed broccoli. Delicious, low carb, and nutrient rich, broccoli makes an excellent side dish for those trying to make healthy dinner choices.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 180mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 385mg 8%
steps: Place the broccoli florets in a steamer basket over a pot of boiling water.
Steam the broccoli for 5–7 minutes or until it is tender-crisp. Remove from heat.
While the broccoli is steaming, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced garlic to the skillet and sauté for 1–2 minutes until it becomes golden brown and crispy. Be careful not to burn the garlic.
Remove the crispy garlic from the skillet and place it on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Place the steamed broccoli in a serving dish.
Drizzle 1 Tbsp of the olive oil over the broccoli and toss to coat.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Sprinkle the crispy garlic and sesame seeds over the steamed broccoli.

title: Steamed Cauliflower with Dill
description: Fresh dill adds bright notes to a simple steamed cauliflower. Low carb and full of nutrients, this side dish makes an excellent choice for a non-starchy veggie side.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 630mg 13%
steps: Bring a medium pot with water and set a steaming basket on top.
Add the cauliflower florets and steam until tender, about 5–7 minutes.
Transfer to a medium bowl and toss with fresh dill, olive oil, salt, and pepper.

title: Sweet Potato Home Fries
description: Whether you are serving them for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, sweet potato home fries are always a family favorite. With tantalizing spices, this recipe will be one you want to make sure you save to make again and again.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 146mg 3%
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into small cubes)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the diced sweet potatoes to the skillet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Sauté the sweet potatoes for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are tender on the inside and crispy on the outside.
Sprinkle the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper over the sweet potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Cook for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the spices to meld with the sweet potatoes.
Remove the skillet from the heat.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Sweet Potato Salad with Cilantro and Lime
description: This Tex-Mex style salad is hearty and filling and sure to rev up your taste buds. It’s diabetes-friendly and would work great as a side dish for your next taco Tuesday dinner!
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 444mg 9%
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into bite-sized cubes)
1 (15 oz) can black beans (Reduced sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
While the sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare the dressing. Zest and juice the lime. In a small bowl, combine chopped fresh cilantro, lime zest, and lime juice.
Once the sweet potatoes are done, transfer them to a serving bowl.
Pour the cilantro and lime dressing over the roasted sweet potatoes.
Add finely chopped red onion, avocado, and black beans to the bowl.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.

title: Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri
description: Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri is a flavorful and satisfying vegetarian dish that transforms cauliflower into hearty steaks and pairs them with a vibrant, zesty chimichurri sauce.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 653mg 14%
ingredients: 1/4 tsp ground red pepper flakes (adjust to taste)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Remove the outer leaves from the cauliflower heads. Trim the stem end to create a flat base.
Cut each cauliflower head into 1-inch-thick slices to create cauliflower steaks.
Place the cauliflower steaks on a baking sheet. Brush both sides with 1 Tbsp olive oil and season with kosher salt and black pepper.
Roast the cauliflower steaks until golden brown and tender, about 20 minutes.

While the cauliflower is roasting, prepare the chimichurri sauce. In a bowl, combine the finely chopped parsley, cilantro, minced garlic, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, red wine vinegar, extra-virgin olive oil, kosher salt and black pepper. Whisk until well-combined.
Once the cauliflower steaks are done, transfer them to serving plates.
Spoon chimichurri sauce generously over each cauliflower steak.

title: Cheesy Sweet Potato and Black Bean Casserole
description: Try this Cheesy Sweet Potato and Black Bean Casserole, a flavorful and hearty dish that brings together the rich sweetness of sweet potatoes, the earthy goodness of black beans, and the gooey comfort of melted cheese. Best of all? This recipe is diabetes-friendly!
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 476mg 10%
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and thinly sliced)
1/4 cup fresh cilantro (Chopped, plus more for garnish if desired)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
In a bowl, combine the sliced sweet potatoes, black beans, corn, diced red onion, and chopped cilantro.
In a small bowl, mix the ground cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, kosher salt, and pepper.
Drizzle the olive oil over the sweet potato mixture and toss to coat.
Sprinkle the spice mixture over the sweet potato mixture and toss again to ensure even coating.
Transfer half of the sweet potato mixture to the prepared baking dish, creating an even layer.
Sprinkle half of the shredded cheddar cheese over the sweet potato layer.
Repeat with the remaining sweet potato mixture and top with the remaining cheese.
Cover the baking dish with foil and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Let the casserole rest for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh cilantro if desired.

title: Curried Tomato Coconut Lentils over Cauliflower Rice
description: This perfectly spiced Curried Tomato Coconut Lentils is a vegetarian dish that is also a nutritious and diabetes friendly option.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 3g 15%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 130mg 6%; Total Carbohydrate 43g 16%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 563mg 12%
ingredients: 1 cup lentils (green or brown, dry, rinsed)
1 (14 oz) can canned diced tomatoes (low sodium)
½ (14 oz) can lite coconut milk
steps: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for an additional 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, and cayenne pepper. Cook the spices with the onion mixture for 1–2 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, and coconut milk to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for 20–25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Serve over the steamed cauliflower rice and garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.

title: Greek Salad with Chickpeas
description: Enjoy the flavors of the mediterranean with this diabetes-friendly version of Greek Salad with Chickpeas. Filled with plant-based protein and fresh vegetables, this is a quick and easy dish that’s filling enough to be a meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 340mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 11g 39%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 871mg 19%
ingredients: 4 med roma (plum) tomatoes (ripe, cut into wedges)
1 (15 oz) can) canned chickpeas (no-salt-added, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a large salad bowl, combine the Romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, red bell pepper, red onion, olives, feta cheese, and chickpeas.
In a small bowl, whisk together the extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, and pepper to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until all ingredients are well coated.

title: Lentil and Vegetable Stir Fry
description: This Lentil and Vegetable Stir-Fry is a wholesome and satisfying vegetarian dish that offers a good balance of protein, fiber, and vitamins from the lentils and colorful vegetables. It's a versatile recipe that allows you to swap in your favorite veggies.
nutrients_raw: Calories 350; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 56g 20%; Dietary Fiber 9g 32%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 20g; Potassium 949mg 20%
ingredients: 1 cup brown lentils (Dry, rinsed and drained)
steps: In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Drain any excess liquid.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and maple syrup. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add broccoli, carrots, red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, and snap peas to the skillet. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Incorporate the cooked lentils into the vegetable mixture.
Pour the prepared sauce over the lentils and vegetables. Stir well to ensure everything is coated in the flavorful sauce.
Continue cooking for an additional 2–3 minutes until everything is heated through.
Garnish with sesame seeds and chopped scallions if desired.

title: Mushroom and Spinach Quesadilla
description: A Mushroom and Spinach Quesadilla is a delicious and quick-to-make dish that combines earthy mushrooms, nutritious spinach, and gooey melted cheese sandwiched between tortillas. It’s a great way to eat more veggies and even the kids will enjoy them.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 24g 9%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 8g; Potassium 181mg 4%
ingredients: 2 cup Mushrooms (of your choice) (sliced, such as cremini or shitake)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms, onions, and minced garlic. Sauté until mushrooms are browned and onions are translucent, about 5–7 minutes. Season with kosher salt and black pepper.
Add the fresh spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Place a tortilla in a dry skillet over medium heat. Sprinkle a portion of both cheeses over half of the tortilla.
Spoon a generous portion of the mushroom and spinach mixture over the cheese.
Fold the tortilla in half, covering the filling, and press it down gently.
Cook the quesadilla on both sides until the tortilla is crispy, and the cheese is melted, about 2–3 minutes per side.
Repeat the process for the remaining tortillas and filling.
Once cooked, cut each quesadilla into wedges and serve.

title: Pasta Fagioli (Italian Pasta and Beans)
description: Pasta e Fagioli, or Pasta Fagioli, is a classic Italian dish that translates to “pasta and beans.” This diabetes-friendly version adds in some nutrient rich veggies for a healthy and satisfying meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 523mg 11%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can canned diced tomatoes (No salt added)
1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans (No salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and sauté for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, cannellini beans, dried oregano, dried basil, dried thyme, kosher salt, and pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and let it simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the shell pasta according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
Add the chopped spinach to the pot and cook until wilted.
Stir in the cooked pasta. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to let the flavors meld. Top with fresh grated parmesan if desired.

title: Red Lentil and Spinach Curry
description: This diabetes-friendly Red Lentil and Spinach Curry is a nutritious meal that combines the earthy flavors of red lentils with the vibrant green goodness of spinach, all infused with aromatic spices in a flavorful curry sauce. Add a bit of chopped fresh cilantro on top for extra flair.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 330mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 42g 15%; Dietary Fiber 9g 32%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 15g; Potassium 555mg 12%
ingredients: 1 (14 oz) can diced tomatoes (No added salt)
1 cup red lentils (dry, rinsed and drained)
steps: In a large pot, heat avocado oil over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, and ginger. Sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and kosher salt to the pot. Stir well to coat the onions with the spices.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juices, coconut milk, and water. Stir to combine.
Add the red lentils to the pot. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20 minutes or until the lentils are tender.
Add spinach leaves to the pot and stir until wilted.

title: Sheet Pan Tofu Fajitas
description: Sheet pan dinners are a quick and easy way to enjoy a nutritious meal without a lot of clean up. This diabetes-friendly tofu fajitas meal is one the whole family will love and uses plant-based protein to keep you full and satisfied.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 31g 11%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 17g; Potassium 187mg 4%
ingredients: 16 oz extra firm tofu (pressed and cubed)
4 whole low carb whole wheat burrito wraps
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Press the tofu to remove excess water, then cut it into cubes.
In a large bowl, combine tofu cubes, sliced bell peppers, and sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, taco seasoning, ground cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, and black pepper to create the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the tofu and vegetables. Toss until everything is evenly coated. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Spread the marinated tofu and vegetables evenly on the sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the tofu is golden and the vegetables are tender, stirring halfway through.
Divide the fajita filling among the wraps.
Serve the sheet pan tofu fajitas and garnish with chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Spaghetti Squash with Tomato Basil Sauce
description: This easy Spaghetti Squash with Tomato Basil Sauce is a great lower-carb option when you are craving pasta. Spaghetti squash makes great substitute noodles that are packed with nutrients, making this a healthy choice for the whole family.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 340mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 911mg 19%
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh basil (Chopped, plus more leaves for garnish)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Cut the spaghetti squash in half lengthwise. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon.
Place the squash halves, cut side up, on a baking sheet. Drizzle each half with 1/2 tbsp olive oil and season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and black pepper.
Roast the spaghetti squash until the flesh is tender and easily shreds into spaghetti-like strands, about 40 minutes.
While the squash is roasting, prepare the tomato basil sauce. In a saucepan, heat 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, basil, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Simmer the sauce for about 15–20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Once the spaghetti squash is done, use a fork to scrape the flesh into spaghetti-like strands.
Serve the spaghetti squash with a generous ladle of tomato basil sauce. Garnish with fresh basil if desired.

title: Stuffed Acorn Squash with Cauliflower Rice
description: This Stuffed Acorn Squash is not only visually appealing but also offers a satisfying combination of textures and flavors. It's a great option for a wholesome and comforting vegetarian meal that’s perfect for a fall weeknight meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 820mg 17%
ingredients: 2 whole acorn squash (halved and seeds removed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Place the acorn squash halves, cut side up, on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil and season with 1/4 tsp kosher salt and black pepper.
Roast the acorn squash in the preheated oven for about 45 minutes to 1 hour or until fork-tender.
While the squash is roasting, prepare the stuffing. In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tsp olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 3–4 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped celery and cook for another 3–4 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add the cauliflower rice, baby spinach, chopped walnuts, dried thyme, dried sage, and remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt. Mix well and cook for an additional 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Once the acorn squash is done roasting, fill each half with the stuffing.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos
description: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos are a delicious and nutritious vegetarian dish that brings together the natural sweetness of sweet potatoes with protein-rich black beans. Try this diabetes-friendly recipe for your next taco night!
nutrients_raw: Calories 330; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 48g 17%; Dietary Fiber 10g 36%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 625mg 13%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans (No salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large mixing bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and minced garlic until evenly coated.
Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes on a baking sheet in a single layer. Roast until the potatoes are tender and slightly crispy, about 20–25 minutes. Stir halfway through the roasting time.
While the sweet potatoes are roasting, heat a skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil, then sauté the chopped red onion until translucent.
Add the black beans to the skillet, stirring to combine with the onions. Cook for an additional 3–5 minutes until the beans are heated through. Season with kosher salt and pepper.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave.
Assemble the tacos by spooning the roasted sweet potatoes and black bean mixture onto each tortilla.
Top each taco with yogurt, cheese, and cilantro.

title: Tofu and Edamame Salad
description: Step into a world of plant-based perfection with our Tofu and Edamame Salad. Silky tofu, vibrant edamame, and a colorful assortment of crisp vegetables create a refreshing symphony of flavors. Tossed in a delightful homemade dressing, this salad invites you to savor the wholesome goodness of each bite.
nutrients_raw: Calories 290; Total Fat 16g 21%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 21g; Potassium 622mg 13%
ingredients: 14 oz firm tofu (firm, pressed and cubed)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the cubed tofu, shelled edamame, thinly sliced red cabbage, julienned carrot, sliced green onions, and sesame seeds.
In a small bowl, whisk together the low-sodium soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, peanut butter, maple syrup, grated fresh ginger, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and gently toss to ensure even coating.

title: Cilantro Lime Rice and Black Bean Bowl
description: Enjoy this Tex-Mex meal that is both vegan and diabetes friendly. Packed with colorful and nutrient-rich veggies, this meal is easy enough to prepare for a healthy weeknight dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 300mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 303mg 6%
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can black beans (No added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the cooked brown rice, black beans, corn, diced red bell pepper, chopped red onion, and fresh cilantro.
In a small bowl, juice the two limes. Add the olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, and kosher salt. Whisk until well combined.
Pour the dressing over the rice and bean mixture. Toss well to ensure even coating.
Allow the flavors to meld for a few minutes before serving.
Top with avocado slices, if desired.

title: Tofu, Mushroom, and Bok Choy Ramen
description: Love ramen? Try this lighter, vegetarian alternative! Add in a dash of sriracha if you prefer your ramen spicy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 34g 12%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 17g; Potassium 357mg 8%
ingredients: 14 oz extra firm tofu (drained, pressed, and cubed)
steps: Cook the ramen noodles according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
In a large pot, heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add sliced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Sauté until the onion is translucent.
Pour in the vegetable broth and water and bring to a simmer.
Add sliced mushrooms, broccoli florets, chopped bok choy, shredded carrots, and cubed tofu to the pot. Simmer for about 5–7 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in coconut aminos and rice vinegar.
Divide the cooked ramen noodles among serving bowls. Ladle the vegetable-rich broth over the noodles and garnish with green onion.

title: Tuna and Avocado Salad
description: Experience a burst of freshness with our Tuna and Avocado Salad, a delightful fusion of flavors and textures. Succulent tuna meets creamy avocado in a salad that would work great as a wrap.
serving_size: 1 cup tuna mixture + 1 cup salad greens
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 17g 22%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 20mg 7%; Sodium 180mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 720mg 15%
ingredients: 2 (5 oz) cans tuna packed in water (drained)
1/3 cup fresh herbs (such as dill, parsley, chopped)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the drained tuna, diced avocados, cucumber, and red onion.
In a smaller bowl, whisk together the extra virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and gently toss to ensure even coating.
Serve on top of the mixed salad greens and fresh herbs.

title: Veggie Pot Pie
description: Filled with delicious and nutritious veggies, this diabetes-friendly pot pie is a healthy alternative the whole family can enjoy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 35g 13%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 14g; Potassium 640mg 14%
ingredients: 2 biscuits Lower-fat buttermilk refrigerated biscuit dough (2-inch, quartered)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
In a large pot, heat the oil on medium heat. Add chopped onion, diced carrots, and diced celery. Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tempeh and potato. Cook for an additional 3–4 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetable mixture and stir to coat evenly. Cook for 1–2 minutes to remove the raw taste of the flour.
Gradually pour in vegetable broth, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Add dried thyme, pepper, and frozen peas. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the filling cool slightly.
Spoon the vegetable filling into a square baking dish.
Top filling with biscuits.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10–15 minutes until biscuits are golden brown. Cut into 4 pieces and serve.

title: Yogurt Ranch Dressing
description: Nothing beats homemade, including ranch dressing! Creamy yogurt adds protein but fresh herbs are the star in this diabetes-friendly salad dressing.

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, chives, parsley, garlic, onion powder, dried dill, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Allow the dressing to sit in the refrigerator for at least 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Zucchini and Corn Fritters
description: These kid-approved Zucchini and Corn Fritters are a fun side dish for a weeknight meal. Try serving it with a dollop of Greek yogurt for dipping!
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 230mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 273mg 6%
ingredients: 2 med zucchini (grated and squeezed to remove excess moisture)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the grated zucchini, corn kernels, whole wheat flour, chopped green onions, minced garlic, beaten eggs, baking powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper. Mix until well combined.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.

Scoop a spoonful of the zucchini and corn mixture and carefully drop it into the hot skillet, flattening it slightly with the back of the spoon to form a fritter. Repeat to make more fritters, ensuring not to overcrowd the skillet.
Cook the fritters for 3–4 minutes on each side or until they are golden brown and cooked through.
Remove the fritters from the skillet and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to absorb any excess oil.
Repeat the process until all the batter is used.
Serve warm.

title: Zucchini Fritters with Feta and Dill
description: Crispy Zucchini Fritters pair great with creamy and bright feta cheese and fresh dill for a delicious side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 40mg 13%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 200mg 4%
ingredients: 2 med zucchini (grated and squeezed to remove excess moisture)
1/2 cup Plain Nonfat Greek yogurt (for serving)
steps: In a bowl, combine the grated and squeezed zucchini, crumbled feta, chopped dill, flour, salt, pepper, and beaten egg.
Form the mixture into 12 small patties and cook them in a skillet with olive oil until golden brown on both sides, about 3 to 5 minutes per side.
Serve with Greek yogurt.

title: Black Bean and Corn Salad
description: Fresh and flavorful, this delicious Black Bean and Corn Salad is a great option when craving Tex-Mex food.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 11g 39%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 8g; Potassium 474mg 10%
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a large mixing bowl, combine black beans, thawed corn, diced red bell pepper, cherry tomatoes, chopped red onion, and fresh cilantro.
Juice the two limes in a small bowl. Add the olive oil, ground cumin, kosher salt, and pepper. Whisk until incorporated.
Pour the dressing over the black bean and corn mixture. Toss well to coat all the ingredients evenly.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Before serving, give the salad a gentle toss. If desired, garnish with additional cilantro and slices of avocado.

title: Beef and Cauliflower Rice Stir Fry
description: With a slight heat from an Asian-inspired homemade sauce, this Beef and Cauliflower Rice Stir Fry is a delicious meal to make for weeknight dinner. Diabetes-friendly and filled with fresh veggies, this is a healthy choice the whole family can enjoy.
serving_size: 1 cup stir fry + 1/2 cup cauliflower rice
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 470mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 20g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 31g; Potassium 1080mg 23%
ingredients: 1 lbs sirloin steak (visible fat removed, frozen for 15 minutes, thinly sliced into 3-inch pieces)
1 tbsp grapeseed oil (or other neutral oil)
1 head broccoli (cut into small florets, about 3 cups)
3 cup cabbage (Red or green, thinly sliced)
2 cup frozen cauliflower rice (Steamed, for serving)
steps: For the marinade, whisk together the baking soda with 2 Tbsp water in a bowl. Coat the beef in the mixture and let it sit for 5–30 minutes in the refrigerator.
To create the sauce, stir together the coconut aminos, hoisin sauce, 1 ½ Tbsp water, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.

Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook until crisp outside but still pink inside, about 2–3 minutes. Stir in 1 Tbsp of the sauce and cook for 30 seconds. Transfer the beef to a plate using a slotted spoon.
Add the carrots, broccoli, cabbage, and bell pepper to the wok, cooking until crisp-tender, about 6 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium, return the beef to the wok, and pour the remaining sauce over the top. Add half of the scallions. Cook for 1 minute.
Divide the steamed cauliflower rice among plates, top with beef and broccoli, ensuring to include all the sauce. Garnish with the remaining scallions.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Chipotle Aioli
description: Roasted Brussels sprouts accompanied by a smoky chipotle aioli make for a bold, diabetes-friendly side dish. Pair it with a simple lean protein like grilled chicken breast for an easy weeknight dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 3g; Potassium 286mg 6%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the Brussels sprouts are golden brown and crispy on the edges.
While the Brussels sprouts are roasting, prepare the aioli.
In a small bowl, combine the mayo, minced chipotle peppers, minced garlic, lime juice, and salt. Mix well.
Once the Brussels sprouts are roasted, transfer them to a serving dish. Serve chipotle aioli on the side.

title: Corn Casserole
description: Enjoy our diabetes-friendly corn casserole, a rich and creamy blend of sweet corn, creamy goodness, creating a warm and hearty dish that's perfect for family gatherings or cozy nights in.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 5g 10%; Protein 4g; Potassium 134mg 3%
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans Canned corn (Whole kernel, drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, combine the whole kernel corn, cream-style corn, cornmeal, diced tomato, Greek yogurt, melted butter, honey, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Pour the corn mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it evenly.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove the casserole from the oven.
Garnish with chopped fresh chives, if desired.
Allow the casserole to cool for a few minutes before serving.

title: Cucumber and Cream Cheese Bites
description: Cucumber and Cream Cheese Bites are a refreshing and easy-to-make appetizer that combines the crispness of cucumber with the creamy goodness of cream cheese. Their crisp texture and the combination of flavors make them a crowd-pleaser, and you can get creative with various toppings to suit your taste preferences like cherry tomatoes or radish slices.
nutrients_raw: Calories 35; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 187mg 4%
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh dill (finely chopped, plus more for garnish)
1 large English cucumber(s) (Sliced into 1/4-inch thin rounds)
steps: In a mixing bowl, blend the cream cheese, finely chopped fresh dill, garlic powder, and lemon zest with a hand mixer until fluffy.
Spread each cucumber well with a generous dollop of the cream cheese mixture.
Garnish with more dill.

title: Korean Lettuce Wraps
description: Korean Lettuce Wraps are a crunchy, lower carb dinner recipe when you’re in the mood for delicious Asian food. Add an extra kick of flavor with Gochujang, Korean red pepper paste, or kimchi.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 20g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 19g; Potassium 328mg 7%
ingredients: 1 head lettuce (such as red oak, green leaf or romaine)
2 tbsp sriracha or gochujang sauce (Korean red pepper paste)
steps: In the bowl of a food processor, pulse the garlic, pear, onion, and ginger until smooth. Transfer the mixture to a medium bowl.

Add the chicken, scallion, soy sauce, sesame oil, and pepper to the bowl. Stir to coat, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. While the chicken marinates, prepare the garnishes and keep the lettuce leaves fresh.
Preheat a large cast iron skillet or sauté pan over high heat.
Add the chicken and any remaining marinade to the hot pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until most of the liquid has evaporated and the chicken is browned, about 10 minutes. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
To serve, place a lettuce leaf in your palm. Add brown rice, chicken, and any desired garnishes. Dab with gochujang, wrap, and enjoy.

title: Kung Pao Chicken and Vegetables
description: Bring bold flavor to dinner with this diabetes-friendly Kung Pao Chicken and Vegetables recipe. Ready in 30 minutes, it’s a great option for a quick weeknight meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 280; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 470mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 27g; Potassium 557mg 12%
ingredients: 1-inch piece fresh ginger (peeled, quartered, and smashed)
2 tbsp Thai style chili garlic sauce
1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into bite-sized chunks)
steps: Whisk together the rice vinegar, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, honey, and cornstarch in a small bowl. Whisk until the cornstarch has dissolved and the sauce is smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the ginger, garlic, and chili-garlic sauce and sauté until fragrant, about 15 seconds.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook and stir until browned and no longer pink inside, 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the bell peppers and cook until slightly softened, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and stir to coat the stir fry. Simmer the sauce until it has thickened and is heated through, about 2 minutes.

title: Blistered Snow Peas with Sesame Seeds
description: Indulge in the crisp perfection of blistered snow peas with sesame seeds, a nutrient-packed, low-calorie option that combines the delicate sweetness of snow peas with the rich, nutty flavor of sesame seeds for a diabetes-friendly side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 45; Total Fat 2g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 86mg 2%
steps: Bring a medium pot with water to a boil and set a steaming basket on top.
Add the snow peas and steam until they turn bright green and become tender.
Drain and toss with mayonnaise, toasted sesame seeds, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.

title: Turkey and Vegetable Scramble
description: This Turkey and Vegetable Scramble recipe is low carb and full of nutrients from fresh veggies, making it a great way to start the day.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 310mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 18g; Potassium 362mg 8%
steps: Heat the canola oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the diced onions and cook until softened.
Add the ground turkey to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spatula. Cook until browned.
Stir in the diced bell peppers and tomatoes, cooking for an additional 2–3 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
Push the turkey and vegetable mixture to the side of the skillet, creating a well.
Pour egg substitute into the well, season with salt and pepper, and scramble until cooked through.
Once the eggs are almost set, mix them with the turkey and vegetables.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the scramble and cover the skillet until the cheese melts.

title: Turkey and Bean Burrito Bowl
description: This Turkey and Bean Burrito Bowl offers a balance of protein, fiber, and fresh ingredients, making it a wholesome and delicious meal. Making a burrito bowl removes the carbs from a tortilla wrap.
nutrients_raw: Calories 310; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 34g; Potassium 780mg 17%
ingredients: 1 cup black beans (Low sodium, drained and rinsed)
1/8 cup Reduced fat Mexican blend cheese (Shredded)
1 whole lime (Cut into wedges for serving)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and cook the ground turkey until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the chili powder, cumin, paprika, kosher salt, and black pepper to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes to toast spices.
Add the bell pepper and onions and cooked until softened. Add in the diced tomatoes and stir well to combine.
Simmer the mixture for about 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the ingredients to heat through.
In a separate skillet, warm the rice and black beans together.
To assemble each bowl, layer ¼ cup brown rice, ¼ cup black beans, ½ cup lettuce, and about ½ cup of the ground turkey mixture.
Top each bowl with about 1 Tbsp of the shredded Mexican blend cheese and chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Zucchini Chips
description: Zucchini chips are a tasty and lighter alternative to traditional potato chips. Enjoy the natural sweetness and texture of zucchini in a crispy form with this diabetes-friendly snack.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 270mg 6%
steps: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a mixing bowl, combine the grated Parmesan cheese, breadcrumbs, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix these dry ingredients well to create a flavorful coating for the zucchini chips.
Thinly slice the zucchinis into rounds. You can use a knife or a mandoline for evenly sliced rounds.
Toss the zucchini slices with the olive oil until they are lightly coated.
Dip each zucchini slice into the prepared coating mixture, making sure both sides are coated evenly.
Place the coated zucchini slices on the baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake in the preheated oven for approximately 20 minutes or until the zucchini chips are golden brown and crispy.

title: Mediterranean Cucumber Salad
description: This creamy Mediterranean Cucumber Salad is a crisp, low-carb side dish that’s perfect for a summer evening.
nutrients_raw: Calories 50; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 118mg 3%
steps: In a bowl, combine the cucumbers, red onion, dill, and pistachios.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the cucumber mixture and toss to coat.

title: Baked Cinnamon Peaches
description: Baked Cinnamon Peaches is a delightful and fresh dessert that enhances the natural sweetness of ripe peaches with warm and cozy cinnamon. For an extra decadent dessert, add a bit of nonfat, frozen yogurt.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 55mg 2%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 290mg 6%
ingredients: 1 1/3 cup frozen yogurt (nonfat, no added sugar)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Cover a 9x9 inch baking dish in parchment paper.
Place the peaches in the baking dish, drizzle with the syrup, and sprinkle with ground cinnamon.
Stir to coat the peaches evenly.
Bake for 30-35 minutes or until the peaches are tender. Serve warm with 1/3 cup of no sugar added frozen yogurt.
Top with the sliced almonds.

title: Berry Salad with Honey, Lime, and Mint
description: Berry Salad with Honey, Lime & Mint is a refreshing and vibrant dish that highlights the natural sweetness of berries with a naturally sweet, zesty topping.
nutrients_raw: Calories 40; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 1g; Potassium 105mg 2%
steps: In a large mixing bowl, combine the strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries.
Zest and juice the lime. In a small bowl, whisk together the lime zest, lime juice, and honey to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the berries, gently tossing to coat.
Allow the berry salad to marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Just before serving, sprinkle the fresh mint over the top of the berry salad and gently toss to incorporate.

title: Cherry Oat Crisp
description: Cherry Oat Crisp is a delightful dessert that combines sweet and tart cherries with a crunchy oat topping. This healthier version is diabetes-friendly so everyone can enjoy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 80mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 256mg 5%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a 9 x 9-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the pitted cherries, lemon juice, zero-calorie maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Toss until the cherries are well coated.
Add the cherries to the prepared baking dish and spread in an even layer.
In a separate bowl, mix the oats, almond flour, chopped nuts, vegetable oil, and salt. Stir until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture evenly over the top of the cherries.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the cherry filling is bubbly, and the oat topping is golden brown.
Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm.
